i have a few preliminary remarks. that's five short points. january 27 marks the 66th anniversary of the liberation of the german nazi concentration and extermination camp auschwitz-birkenau. every year on this day, we honor the memory of over a million people who were murdered there. it gives us the strength to build together a peaceful future for a united europe that will not have such nightmares in the future. second information: on january 13, the lithuanian nation celebrated the 20th anniversary of bloody sunday, when the soviet army attempted to overthrow the democratically elected government of independent lithuania. lithuanians defended their freedom and are today equal members of the euro-atlantic community. as we mark this important anniversary for europe, we stand in solidarity with the people of belarus, including our neighbours, who are still waiting for freedom and democracy to come to their country. other information: the european union acceded to the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities on 23 december 2010. this convention, together with the disability strategy prepared by the european commission, will ensure that by 2020 almost 80 million citizens of the union with different types of disabilities enjoy equal civil, political and economic rights. information number four: i would also like to remind you that we are deeply concerned about the disappearance of mr. gao zhisheng's chinese lawyer. according to the latest information, he is being mistreated and tortured. the european parliament has already dealt the president. - dear colleagues! we have been watching with great concern and hope the events in tunisia over the past few weeks. peaceful demonstrations in defence of legitimate demands turned into bloody clashes - which we regret - as the tunisian authorities turned against their own citizens. today we bow our heads before the victims of these events. our deepest sympathies go out to all those who have lost loved ones. we remember in particular the first victim of the clashes, the young mohammed bouazizi. this tragic gesture has become a symbol of the wave of democratic reaction in tunisian society. let us all take a moment of silence in memory of our tunisian friends. please rise. (silence for a minute) thank you very much. thank you. dear colleagues! the jasmine revolution is underway. in many ways, this is a truly historic time. i want to express my deep appreciation for the courage and determination of the people of tunisia. they're the source of these changes. but this is only the beginning of a long journey. as europeans, we share the tunisian people's aspirations and want to accompany them on their journey towards their full realization. europeans are particularly sensitive to social justice, equal opportunities, freedom of expression, democracy and genuine pluralism, shaping their own political future. that's why we're not going to sit idly by today. we call for these changes to be peaceful. they must lead to justice and the rule of law. we also have fundamental postulates. first, the release of all arbitrarily arrested. second, to conduct independent investigations into serious allegations of corruption, as well as cases of death, abuse of power. thirdly, transparent, genuinely democratic presidential and parliamentary elections, monitored by local and foreign observers, and fourthly, we support efforts to create a government of national unity that represents all tunisians. the european union and tunisia have a longstanding partnership, they are our neighbours across the mediterranean. this partnership must be primarily for the benefit of our citizens, the tunisians and the europeans. our partnership, if it is to remain credible and meaningful, must support the tunisian people in their journey towards profound change. we have to help tunisia succeed. dear colleagues! let's side with the tunisians.

madam president! we're dealing with a scandal, but a scandal is too small a word. this is a major threat to the lives and health of thousands of people. i hope that the culprits will be found and punished, but let this case also be a reason to reflect on the model of agriculture that we have created in the european union. agriculture has become an industry. we're no longer raising animals, we're producing meat, we have big farms, we have a feed industry and animals fed with feed, and with dioxins, genetically modified feed, not fully tested, and this model of agriculture is not working. this is a model that doesn't guarantee food security. the solution is to have more respect for the farms that we still have in europe, in poland and in other countries, which are based on their own feed production. we should support it.
madam president! last month, i was in the republic of congo with a delegation from the development committee, where we also discussed the flegt initiative with representatives of the authorities, experts and ngos. the timber industry is a very important industry for this country. it's the second largest source of export revenue after oil. it is worth recalling that what happens to oil revenues and their use is not completely transparent and clear to us, or at least the information is transmitted with a long delay. at the same time, the government of the republic of congo is expressing concern about the future of forest areas and is planning a major reforestation campaign. of course, we don't know yet if this afforestation program will succeed, but it's certainly worth wishing the congolese government that it will. that's why it's so important to strengthen the legal timber trade. it is equally important that flegt operates in neighbouring countries, because otherwise, for example through smuggling, the agreement may not be effective in practice. and we don't know yet whether the standards we're promoting for legal timber trade will become global and functional. we must make sure that this system works. we also need to help put pressure on other importers (outside europe) to phase out the illegal timber trade. flegt is important for reducing poverty, protecting the environment, curbing deforestation and developing diversified economies in many countries. in the case of the republic of congo, this goes hand in hand with another need, namely the need to develop agriculture and reduce food imports. flegt has the potential to make global trade in timber fairer, more sustainable and more environmentally friendly. we hope that's what happens.

mr. chairman, please! adoption can and often does benefit a child, but the procedures involved can also be a source of abuse, such as child trafficking or the taking of children for adoption from families that have not abandoned their children but are often unable to provide them with the right conditions because of poverty. the large number of children in orphanages that we are talking about in today's debate are often not abandoned children, but children of poor parents who are not able to cope with the difficult situation of life. we have to help families like that. states could spend far less money to help these families, without putting them in orphanages and, consequently, for adoption. we should adopt a clear rule - in the european union, it should be the rule - never take children from their families because of poverty, help, don't take children. poverty can't be a reason to take a child away from his birth family.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your work. i am very pleased that the european parliament is dealing today with the issue of adoption within the union, because it is a matter which is very close to my heart. the special reference to children in the charter of fundamental rights and in article 3 of the treaty on european union gives us the opportunity, but also the obligation, to address this issue. international adoption can be a chance for a normal life and family happiness for many abandoned children who, due to their age or health conditions, do not have the opportunity to adopt in their own countries. in europe today, we have a situation where there are few children available for adoption in countries where abortion is widely available and widely promoted. in other lands, there are many, and only the youngest have the opportunity to start their own families. additionally, an increasing number of couples are having difficulty conceiving their own children or are suffering from incurable infertility. i therefore welcome the work of the european commission in this area with great enthusiasm. member states should agree on simplifying procedures which are not too complex and time-consuming. but we must not forget that we have to put in place protective and control mechanisms to prevent the trafficking of children.

member of the commission. − mr president, i very much welcome mrs striffler’s report, as well as parliament’s involvement in and continued strong advocacy for effective european humanitarian action. the consensus was adopted in 2007. it provides an essential common policy framework for the eu – a common vision accompanied by an action plan. both the member states and the commission have a shared responsibility to make sure that the consensus is well implemented. i want to stress that what comes very clearly out of the report is the message that humanitarian principles, international humanitarian law and protection of the humanitarian space have to be at the centre of our action on the consensus. four-fifths of our humanitarian aid goes to people in need in conflict-related, man-made emergencies. for us to be able to reach these people it is critical that our aid is independent and neutral and that it is perceived in this way. i would like to give you one example of this. i have just come back from yemen where, together with the un high commissioner for refugees, antonio gutierrez, we engaged on the humanitarian access issue with high-level government officials and representatives of the al-houthi rebel movement. for the first time we obtained commitment on their part to facilitate humanitarian access and respect delivery of aid to all yemeni people in need, in line with the humanitarian principles of neutrality and independence. having spent a number of hours with men with kalashnikovs, i would like to observe that we in europe do bring this value of neutrality that is a bridge to people in need. in the yemeni case, there are 300 000 internally displaced people and many more hundred thousands affected by six wars in six years in the north of yemen. of course, for a long-lasting impact, humanitarian aid is not the right instrument. it is development that can lay the foundation for lasting peace. we in the commission have completed a year-long review process of the european consensus action plan, in close liaison with our member state and humanitarian partners. on 8 december, the commission adopted a communication on this. the review shows that over the past three years we have made significant contributions to strengthening the humanitarian response in terms of advocacy and humanitarian action, as well as by bringing humanitarian aid and civil protection together. we also concluded that there is scope for further improvement in three areas. firstly we need to promote the quality and effectiveness of aid by good assessment, a well-coordinated response and investment in disaster risk reduction and local capacity. at a time when needs are growing and budgets are constrained, this is critical. let me just respond here to the question of accountability. obviously we need to stretch every euro to the full and deliver it with the highest possible quality and in the most effective way. in order to ensure that our partners – un agencies and ngos – are accountable, we review one-third of all partners and one-third of all projects every year. we have our own humanitarian aid offices in all the hotspot areas of the planet to be the ears and the eyes of our taxpayers, including in yemen, because of increasing humanitarian needs. i recently cut the ribbon of our humanitarian aid office there. the second issue concerning which we can see room for improvement is the strengthening of the european voice. we are the largest donor and have to make sure that we speak very clearly with one voice. we must also reach out to other donors so that we play our leadership role, vis-à-vis traditional donors, but also by engaging new donors. thirdly we need to ensure coherence which means working, together with the external action service, with military actors to make sure that a principled humanitarian approach is safeguarded and is also promoted in europe. let me finish by once again thanking mrs striffler for her work on this issue and calling upon parliament to continue the discussion on this topic. the world has changed. unfortunately there will be more and more natural and man-made disasters. whatever action we take will determine not only the lives of the people affected, but also the moral standing and the capacity of the eu to lead in the world.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday, 18 january 2011. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
in writing. humanitarian aid is a manifestation of universal solidarity between people, it is our moral duty. today, we see a steady increase in the need for humanitarian aid because of the increasing number of natural disasters being reported. climate change is not the only factor, but so are the developments in disaster detection and communication technologies. the key criteria for delivering humanitarian aid should be speed, accountability and the lowest possible administrative costs. the development of transport is a factor in facilitating aid delivery. this will allow more victims to be reached and assisted more quickly. this is why it is so important to involve companies corporations, groups, but also small businesses (not only transport and logistics) in building a network of actors working together in the field to deliver aid effectively and to improve the rapid response system to threats. based on a cross-sector partnership (business - organisation/institution), bases, branches, offices with funds, storage space, volunteers, food, necessary materials and equipment and means of transport can be created. such cooperation can bring tangible benefits in the face of human tragedy, especially when there is a need to respond quickly rather than to fundraising first.
mr. chairman, please! i also join in congratulating mrs sârbu on her excellent report, which i consider to be one of the most important of this term. the world's population is growing, but the land is shrinking. food is becoming a strategic commodity more and more. while solar and nuclear energy can replace oil, nothing can replace food from the earth. in the european union, we sometimes act as if we were constantly faced with the problem of overproduction of food. the whole agricultural policy of the european union in recent years has been about how to limit agricultural production, how to reduce it. today, there are already times of food shortage on the horizon. it is very good that the signal is coming from parliament, thanks to mrs sârbu's report, that the situation has changed and that the european union's agricultural policy must change too. we must respect agriculture as the guarantee of our food security.
in writing. dear colleagues! europe needs a common agricultural policy that will ensure the development, not the stagnation, of european agriculture. agricultural policy must respond to european and global challenges, especially when we consider that according to the world food and agriculture organisation, food production must increase by at least 70% to meet the world's population, which is expected to exceed 9 billion by 2050. it is therefore clear that the cap should increase food security by increasing productivity while promoting an environmentally sustainable food policy. i would like to point out that the rules in this area should be transparent. i appreciate the initiatives that encourage the promotion of agricultural diversity, including traditional and organic farming. in addition, it is important to guarantee young farmers access to land and credit to pursue cap objectives such as innovation, modernisation, enhanced competitiveness and, above all, modern agriculture.

in writing. to sum up the belgian presidency, the first thing to be acknowledged is its very active role in designing the european financial stability system. anyone who has observed this process knows that it was a difficult and time-pressured operation. i therefore warmly congratulate all those who have contributed to this project. in this area, the belgian presidency leaves the hungarian presidency with a task well accomplished. it should also be noted that the belgians set the course for the future presidencies in the context of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. i would like to express the hope that the successive presidencies, including the polish one, will make greater efforts to set clear priorities of their own, which are nevertheless in line with our common european objectives. this way of working makes it easier to plan and implement the policies of the european institutions.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen! i would like to begin by congratulating the belgian presidency on its excellent presidency of the council of the european union over the last six months. the success of the belgian team is enhanced by the circumstances in which the country has taken the lead. firstly, it was the first presidency to act on the basis of the principles established by the lisbon treaty, and secondly, the financial situation of the union and its individual member states was very difficult. in addition, during the belgian presidency, the country had to deal with internal problems. despite this difficult and demanding period, the presidency has been effective and has conducted all its activities in a european style. it has put its internal problems (issues) aside and focused on implementing the line set by the european parliament, the european commission and the council of the european union and on supporting these institutions. the presidency has accepted the role of mediator. the commission's priorities include measures to combat the economic crisis, particularly the work on the next multiannual financial framework. another significant achievement of the belgian presidency is the issue of the euro vignette. in conclusion, i would like to say that the belgian presidency can be a good lesson for the next countries to take over the presidency of the council of the european union. i would also like to wish the same success to the hungarian presidency and to the polish presidency, which will begin in mid-2011.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen! i would like to thank the belgian presidency for its past role as a model for the countries that will take over the presidency of the council of the eu in the future. this is a subject which is particularly close to my heart in the face of the forthcoming polish presidency, which i hope will make use of all the positive paths that have been traced under belgian leadership. it is not often that the presidency puts its own internal interest ahead of community action. the most important success of this presidency, in my view, has been the consistent implementation of the lisbon treaty, particularly at the level of the european council, which has become a full institution with a permanent president, and at the level of the foreign affairs council, which is currently headed by the high representative. the fight against the economic crisis has also proved to be important: systematic control and restraint of the financial sector will help to stabilise its fragile status over time, especially at a time when the pressure to develop the euro area is so great. in conclusion, i sincerely hope that the path set out during the belgian presidency will be a model of quality for the countries taking over the presidency in the future. let the good of the commonwealth always be our first priority. thank you, sir.
mr. chairman, please! the construction sector is a very important part of any country's economy. in pursuing economic growth and improving the standard of living of citizens, such an important part of the market cannot be ignored. everyone knows how important a properly constructed or upgraded facility is to safety and comfort. at the same time, we all want to reduce the cost of building homes, industrial buildings, public buildings. the report aims to remove market barriers, allow for smooth trade in construction goods and ensure competitive prices in the sector. the whole of europe will benefit from this initiative. i also fully support the author's demands for greater safety for workers in this industry.
mr. chairman, please! our role as members of the european parliament is to work for the betterment of the citizens of the union. providing them with access to safe food of the highest quality should be a top priority. food shortages and high food prices are usually associated with social unrest and we cannot allow this to happen on our continent. with a growing population, climate change, and natural disasters, global food security is at risk. so many people are starving already. to remedy this, a sound and fair common agricultural policy and financial support for the sector are necessary. agriculture should be granted a special status to allow for specific actions and appropriate instruments to be used in the event of possible food crises.
in writing. − african countries with particularly difficult geographical and climatic conditions require special treatment. but these people don't just need food and water, they also need education, they want to work with dignity and they want to move. the european union agreement with the economic and monetary union of west africa, replacing certain provisions of previous agreements, significantly facilitates and makes air transport procedures between the parties to the agreement more fair in the market. this will prevent unfair practices by monopolists and make it easier for ordinary citizens to move around. these are also new opportunities for tourists from all over the world and the associated development of this sector in africa.
in writing. − the functioning of the internal market is still limited by numerous barriers. i therefore welcome the adoption of the regulation on the placing on the market of construction products. this regulation should contribute to facilitating the movement of construction goods between member states. the regulation also introduces important provisions to facilitate business. first, it requires member states to set up product contact points where traders can obtain information on construction products. it also contains provisions to help the smallest enterprises to meet the new requirements for the production of declarations of performance and ce marking. however, we should not forget that the provisions of the regulation include a number of new obligations relating to the requirement to affix the ce marking and to the drawing up of a declaration of performance, which will also have to contain information on dangerous substances contained in construction products. i hope that the european commission and the member states will do their utmost to ensure that producers are informed of the new rules as soon as possible so that they can start preparing and adapting to the new regulation as soon as possible.
in writing. - one year after the earthquake in haiti, we can see that the actions we take, or the way we help, are not perfect. the european consensus on improving humanitarian aid delivery must not be allowed to lapse. the union, as one of the richest and most developed regions in the world, has a moral obligation to help the weak and needy. we must especially show solidarity with the victims of disasters and natural disasters who are not prepared for what is coming. all efforts should therefore be made to strengthen cooperation between member states in this area and to facilitate the sharing of good practice. we must make sure that the aid system is efficient and effective and that not a penny is wasted. cooperation with other actors, ngos or international organisations also involved in such assistance is therefore necessary to make it as effective as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the sârbu report on the recognition of agriculture as a strategic sector in the context of food security. food security has historically been one of the most important responsibilities of any authority. the financial or economic criterion cannot therefore be decisive. producing cheap, good food is very important for the market and the purchasing power of the population, especially the low-income population. but even more important is the ability to produce food. we cannot afford to rely on food imports just because someone can sell it to us cheaply on a regular basis. we can import, but we also have to maintain our own capacity to produce the amount of food we need.
in writing. −food security is a key challenge for agriculture not only in the european union but also around the world, especially in developing countries. according to the fao, by 2050, global food demand will double, and the world's population will increase from the current 7 billion to 9 billion. world food production will therefore have to increase accordingly in the face of natural resource pressures. world food production will have to increase with less water, energy, fertilizer and pesticide use and less land. the number of hungry people in the world is over a billion, and more than 40 million poor people in the european union lack enough food to eat. i therefore believe that scientific progress should be used if it can provide the appropriate solutions to alleviate world hunger, in particular through more efficient use of resources. the eu must continue to ensure food security for its citizens and contribute to the world's food supply, while working better and more coherently with the rest of the world, in particular developing countries, to help them develop their agricultural sectors in a sustainable way in the long term. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the recognition of agriculture as a strategic sector in the context of food security.
in writing. - i am convinced that the recognition of agriculture as a strategic sector will create better conditions for the implementation of assistance and information programmes. there is certainly a need to develop food aid programmes for the poorest. we often forget that in the european union, nearly 80 million people live below the poverty line. in addition to the aid programmes, programmes should be developed to promote healthy eating, especially among school children and young people. the effects of this neglect are most evident in the united states, where the number of overweight teenagers has tripled in recent years. the presence of programmes in educational establishments promoting fruit and milk consumption is particularly important, as well-formed eating habits will have a positive impact on the health of young europeans and thus reduce subsequent health and social expenditure. such programmes should involve as many local food producers and distributors as possible, thereby strengthening the position of small and medium-sized farms.

president of the commission. − mr president, i would like, first of all, to thank ms wortmann-kool. in fact, this is not just my position but the unanimous position of the commission. it says in this document, about the annual growth survey, that the commission considers that the effective financing capacity of the european financial stability facility (efsf) must be reinforced and the scope of its activity widened. we consider this as part of a comprehensive response and not, of course, as the entire response. there is only one sentence in this document about the efsf. it is also about structural reform, fiscal consolidation and growth-enhancing measures. but, in fact, it is important for the stability of the euro area to increase lending capacity because, as you know, the efsf is currently endowed with eur 440 billion. i am not asking now for this ceiling to be increased, but we know that the efsf cannot, de facto, lend this eur 440 billion if need be, due to the need to secure a triple-a rating for the efsf. so the minimum we can and should do is to increase the capacity of the fund. i think this is a very constructive proposal that should be adopted sooner rather than later.
president of the commission. − mr president, ‘sooner rather than later’ means precisely that: that we should not procrastinate. we have seen in the past that many analysts in the market consider the european union and the euro area to be reacting rather than acting. we need to be ahead of the curve, not behind the curve, so as soon as possible it shall be! in fact, it seems that the euro area meeting yesterday and today’s ecofin meeting made some progress. we are contacting our member states. i believe that is important. and i think it will be wise, since we have the european council on 4 february, to address these issues there. we are ready to do so. the commission is ready to address these issues on 4 february.

president of the commission. − the focus is not only on the labour market. we are reforming the financial markets with the active support and participation of this parliament. we also discussed at length the need to deepen internal market reform in the annual growth survey. we are now specifically discussing energy markets, but the labour market is also part of the structural reforms needed to increase europe’s competitiveness, especially in those countries that are now most vulnerable. as you know, some of them are already undertaking important labour market reforms.

president of the commission. − mr president, i should point out that the european court of auditors is a fully independent body. the commission has absolutely no influence over its methods or audit priorities, nor would we seek to have that kind of influence. it is in the commission’s own interest, and in the european interest, to respect the independence of its external auditor. i have never made negative comments about decisions of courts, be it the constitutional courts, the european court of justice or the court of auditors. that is a basic principle of democracy, respect for the rule of law and respect for independent institutions. a regular dialogue exists, of course, between the commission as auditee and the court as auditor, as part of the audit process. this is normal and necessary to ensure the audit process works well and that all findings in the audit process are on a solid basis. such a dialogue is fully in accordance with all international standards. i should probably also point out that in previous years the commission was subject to extremely critical reports from the court of auditors. i think we should respect our institutions, namely the independent institutions.

president of the commission. − mr president, you cut the honourable member off just when he was saying something nice about me, for which i thank him. regarding the first part of his intervention, we do not have the means – and it is not our priority now – to explore, or support the exploration of, other sources of energy in europe. our priority in terms of infrastructure is to establish interconnections, because that has a critical european dimension. we are going to make proposals on that matter to the european council. something has been achieved already – for instance bemip, the baltic energy market interconnection plan, for the baltic countries. now we are working also with central and eastern european countries to establish, if possible, north-south interconnections, and things are going well. i have just been to azerbaijan and turkmenistan in connection with work on the southern gas corridor, a new potential means of bringing energy – in this case gas – to europe. this is where i believe the european union can make some investments in energy infrastructures.
president of the commission. − as you said, it is correct that eur 200 billion of investment is needed for gas infrastructures and power grids up to 2020. it is estimated that eur 100 billion of this total investment need will be delivered on time by the market alone, whereas the other eur 100 billion will require public action on permitting and leveraging the necessary private capital. that is why we are now proposing, for instance, unbundling. we are proposing many measures that will make this private investment more rational and more useful. we will also take a closer look at tariff regulation practices in order to liberate adequate cost allocation principles. to fill the remainder of the gap, the commission proposes a new financial instrument to support projects of european interest for the new financial perspective after 2013. beyond grants, innovative market-based solutions may be proposed such as equity participations, guarantees and public-private partnership loans. as you know, i already spoke about european funds through project bonds specifically designed for this kind of project.

president of the commission. − you know the position of the commission regarding nuclear energy. with full respect for subsidiarity in that matter, some member states have it and some do not. no one is forced to have nuclear energy, but in fact it is true that nuclear energy is, in terms of climate change, less polluting than other sources of energy. having said that, the commission has certain obligations under the euratom treaty. at the beginning of the european union we had the euratom community, and the commission has not only the right but also the duty to provide assistance to member states that require it in the fields of nuclear safety or research into nuclear matters. that is certainly what we intend to do.

president of the commission. − the internal energy market legislation sets high standards of consumer protection with regard to the provision of a minimum service, transparency of billing, effective complaint handling and so on, and it provides choices to consumers. i could quote many other areas in which we are proposing measures that directly address consumers’ concerns. regarding lower energy bills, we think that, in the medium term at least, in a real integrated energy market, true competition can achieve more than the current situation, in which there are many dysfunctions and examples of dominant market positions. regarding funding for energy security projects, as i said earlier, we certainly intend to propose it in the next financial perspectives. so part of it has to come from market solutions, but part of it has to come from public investment. the european commission is preparing some proposals that will move in this direction for the next financial perspectives.

mr. chairman, please! there are no perfect laws. there are advantages and disadvantages everywhere, but this directive definitely brings more hope than fear. europe, despite its rapid change, remains a continent of great differences and even contrasts. this also applies to the level and scale of healthcare, and it is evident that poorer countries, countries in transition and emerging countries are more concerned. but the level of funding and the level of health care in countries that are in transition is much, much lower. so this directive represents a huge opportunity and hope for all these patients in the countries i'm talking about. governments face a great challenge, but paradoxically, this directive will force many reforms and will draw attention to the scale of underfunding of healthcare, because underfunding is not only the result of these countries' lack of financial capacity, but also the result of policy errors and a misunderstanding of the enormous importance of health to european citizens. i thank you and i appeal to you to support this directive, whatever the final shape of the so-called safeguard clause, which is a compromise. and that word is good news.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to begin by congratulating mrs grossetête, who has done a very difficult job. this was not an easy task, given the different positions of the european union countries and the different health systems in each country. to achieve a compromise between expectations and possibilities, it was necessary not only to have the ability to negotiate, but above all to have knowledge of the subject. we are all aware that the solutions contained in the directive on patients' rights in crossborder healthcare, which the rapporteur has spoken about in detail, are awaited by the people of the european union, especially in those countries where access to specialist doctors and modern procedures is limited. it is important that the work on the text of the directive and the compromises reached have changed the attitude of the countries that originally blocked its entry. the essence of this directive is the accessibility, ease and certainty of healthcare, as well as the right of the patient to use healthcare services of another country and to be reimbursed for certain costs. the directive is based on the needs of the patient, not on financial means. i would like to point out that the provisions of the directive will not only improve the health situation of patients, but i believe that it will also be the basis for improving health systems in some countries of the european union. it should be stressed that the directive is a first and fundamental step towards patient mobility, towards strengthening their rights and towards equalising the level of services in the various member states.
in writing. the entry into force of the patients without borders directive is a great opportunity for all patients in the european union, but especially for patients from less developed countries whose health services have much to offer. they will have better access to treatment abroad than ever before. it is also hoped that the new solutions will be the impetus for changes in national healthcare systems. this is especially true for reducing long queues for people waiting for various types of hospital treatment. the risk of outflows to foreign clinics will force administrative decisions on better management of hospital beds and treatments in countries with longer queues. the obligation for patients to set up contact points in each eu country is important, as this will give patients more information about treatment options abroad or the achievements of foreign clinics in the treatment of rare or very serious diseases. it is important that, once the new rules have entered into force, their effects, their impact on improving the quality of services, but also on accessibility for different groups of patients in different regions of europe, are closely monitored. first of all, who benefits from them: whether it's just the better informed, more resourceful social groups or everyone in need.
mr. chairman, please! as the population of the european union ages, the proportion of people suffering from old age diseases is increasing. statistics show that one in five people over the age of 80 suffers from alzheimer's disease. not everyone knows that it is an incurable disease, but with proper prevention and early diagnosis, its effects can be delayed. according to the 2009 world alzheimer's report, 28% of people with dementia live in europe, the second largest dementia population in the world after asia. in poland, the country i represent, there are about 250,000 people with alzheimer's disease, and experts estimate that by 2040, that number will triple. as you can see, these numbers are disturbing. dementia has both social and economic consequences, affecting not only the patient but also those close to him. so i'm glad we're addressing this important issue today. only cooperation, highly specialised research and a broad information campaign will allow for faster diagnosis and better prevention.

member of the commission. − dear colleagues, i am pleased to report that both parts of the european progress microfinance facility – the guarantees part and the cash products part – are now entirely operational. only three months after the entry into force of the decision, the commission finalised the mandate for the european investment fund to launch the guarantee operations for microfinance providers. last november the commission established a specialised investment vehicle. as a result, the first micro-loans will be provided starting from this month. i am also pleased to report that the commission has been successful in securing additional funding for micro-entrepreneurs in europe. the european investment bank will match the european union’s contribution of eur 100 million, and further contributors are expected. as a result, the overall volume of loans under the progress microfinance facility will amount, as planned, to around eur 500 million. this money will benefit unemployed people, people facing social exclusion or vulnerable persons who face difficulties in accessing the conventional credit market. ensuring outreach to these target groups and promoting geographical balance are key elements of the mandate given by the commission to the european investment fund. operations approved so far, or under preparation, suggest that both objectives will be met. as from early 2011, micro-loans will be provided through a start-up microfinancing institution in belgium which focuses on disadvantaged urban communities, and through a foundation in the 40% are expected to involve intermediaries investing in europe and about 60% in central and eastern europe. it is well known that microfinance is most effective if business starters and micro-enterprises are accompanied through business support services. as such, the commission will undertake measures to support european social fund managing authorities and intermediate bodies to entrepreneurs can also be supported through interest rebates. however, whether or not interest rebates are subsidised through the esf is a decision to be taken by the individual member states. at present only one member state, namely lithuania, has indicated that it makes use of this possibility. lastly, the commission will promote information about the progress microfinance facility. the microfinance providers who are closest to the target beneficiaries will provide information on the availability of micro-loans. the commission will make use of existing networks of public employment services, esf managing authorities and ngos to provide information on the progress of the microfinance facility. last but not least, the youth on the move campaign will pay special attention to madam president! the european union has not forgotten haiti. we are by far the largest source of humanitarian aid. what is depressing is that the country is still in economic and political chaos. humanitarian aid in haiti has been delivered in two classic phases. the first phase of the relief effort was to provide relief to people in their most urgent needs. in the second phase, we were to focus on the reconstruction of the country, both economically and sociopolitically. but because of the cholera epidemic, the hurricane, the political and social instability, and even the interfaith tensions and fighting, the humanitarian relief period has been longer than we originally expected. it was therefore not possible to proceed to this second stage either to the extent and at the pace that we would have liked. the crisis in haiti is still going on. we need to be involved all the time. we can't forget about our commitments. the commissioner also pointed out that the european commission had already committed half the funds promised at the donor conference in new york. in this respect, our plans are progressing well. the resolution we are adopting tomorrow in this house is intended to mobilise the member states and the commission to continue to fulfil the declarations we have made. let's not forget that hundreds of thousands of people are still living in makeshift camps, and more than 3,500 people have died of cholera. and from the very beginning, we also felt that the rebuilding process should be hosted by the haitian people themselves. the haitian reconstruction plan is based on decentralisation and a strong focus on local agricultural production and food security. we respect those haitian priorities. there is one more conclusion. we need to strengthen our humanitarian response capabilities, and i know the commissioner is already working on that.
madam president! a year ago, haiti was hit by a terrible cataclysm, a massive earthquake, which killed 200,000 people, leaving over 1,300,000 homeless. the relief and reconstruction efforts have been going on for a year. this is undoubtedly a large and very complex humanitarian operation. but the island needs not only material and financial assistance, but also the rebuilding of its administration and political stability, without which it cannot develop. moreover, the recent cholera epidemic, which has killed over 3,500 people, continues to threaten thousands. the experience of haiti shows that even large amounts of money will not help if not spent properly. the case of haiti should also be a sobering one, and it clearly shows the need for a well-functioning international aid system in the event of major natural disasters, which may also occur.
madam president! it will be almost a year since our last discussion on coordinating humanitarian aid and reconstruction in haiti. so today we're doing some sort of summary, and the conclusion is this: it's been a year since the tragedy, and the victims are still coming. there are two things that need to be emphasized here that are just as important, if not more important, than building new houses, new roads. first, we need to say, loud and clear, in this room, "stop the sexual violence epidemic". sources say that in the days following the earthquake, 250 rapes of women and girls were reported, and the situation is getting worse. this violence is escalating. it is high time to start speaking out about this shameful issue and to address this inhuman phenomenon and to start fighting sexual violence in haiti effectively. the second issue that has already been mentioned here is the cholera epidemic. the number of cases is decreasing, but it's obviously related to the time of year. and there's an interesting but disturbing phenomenon with patients who are faking cholera symptoms. it's hard for us to believe that we're going to spend the night in comfortable beds, but for these people, a night in a hospital is much better than a night in their own homes, and in fact, in a shack. and here, too, we should pay attention, especially since the cholera epidemic is sure to intensify with the change of seasons. we must therefore pay attention to this and we should improve the situation here in particular.
madam president! i'd like to be understood. i have no serious complaints about the current european union aid to haiti. the union does provide substantial material aid to haiti, and it is surprising that many other countries do not do so on the scale of the union. i would like to remind you that our reservations were raised by the union's action immediately after the disaster. the union was too slow to act, and humanitarian aid was clearly poorly coordinated. i would therefore like to ask what concrete conclusions the european commission drew from this aid, which was very slow at the time. i think this is a very important thing, because the timing of getting help is a matter of life or death for some people.
madam president! the situation in lithuania today is one of the right of any democratically elected government to freely legislate in its own country and the obligation to respect human rights protected by eu law and international conventions. the role of the european parliament is undoubtedly, among other things, to draw attention to all cases where human rights are violated, also because of belonging to different social groups. parliament has adopted resolutions on these issues on several occasions. he was always against violating those laws. today's debate is also the result of concerns that the draft amendment to lithuanian law may lead to restrictions on freedom of expression in lithuania on the basis of sexual orientation, for example. this concern is justified in the sense that the issue of the discriminatory treatment of human rights in lithuania by the lithuanian authorities has been raised on several occasions in the european parliament. i am thinking here first of all of the national minorities, who are unfortunately not treated equally by lithuanian law in terms of the rights they are granted. it is therefore worth stressing that draft national legislation must meet certain standards and be in line with eu law, which guarantees equal treatment for defined minorities, including national ones.

madam president! i voted in favour of the directive presented by mrs grossetête, so that after long negotiations the principles of crossborder treatment in the european union can finally be put into practice. i regard the directive as a good compromise in its present form, based mainly on the rights of the patient, but also safeguarding the interests of the national health funds of the member states. for citizens of countries such as poland, the possibility of receiving treatment abroad equalises access to modern healthcare. overcrowded hospitals, long queues, waiting lists for some major procedures often leave patients without access to timely, appropriate health care. in some cases, time plays a huge role. the directive will allow citizens to decide for themselves whether to wait for treatment in their own country for many months or to choose another place of treatment. knowing that a treatment in another eu country will also be reimbursed, if only in large part, and sometimes even in full, will make it easier for them to decide on the treatment. the simplification of treatment rules abroad can of course also be seen as triggering market forces in general access to medical services. these solutions will therefore, in my view, contribute to increasing competitiveness in healthcare and, therefore, also have a significant impact on accelerating the growth of these services.
madam president! european society is becoming increasingly mobile. we study, work, rest and travel outside our own country. citizens living in the community should have the right to free emergency medical care wherever they are in europe. it is clear that instruments should be put in place to prevent so-called health tourism, making it easier for patients in need to take advantage of new opportunities. first of all, i'm talking about the treatment of unusual rare diseases in specialized centers, sometimes outside the country where the patient lives. but we cannot allow interference in the form of health policy pursued by the member states. this is their internal competence and they are free to do so. this directive is moving in that direction. of course i voted yes.

madam president! alzheimer's is one of the diseases for which mankind still has no cure. the medical services data show a frightening increase in the number of cases diagnosed, and the trend of an ageing europe has drastic consequences for the near future. dementia affects not only the person but also his or her family, who often have to sacrifice their own lives to care for their loved ones. we urgently need these kinds of reports that identify the problem and suggest initiatives to improve the quality of our health and lives. the joint efforts of the community countries, the creation of programmes of prevention and social support for whole families are, of course, projects worthy of all the support. we need to do everything we can to help those who are suffering and to minimize the number of future cases.
in writing. − the crossborder healthcare directive is a very important new legal instrument that can significantly improve the situation of patients in the european union. today, patients who want to receive medical care in a country other than their own face many administrative and financial obstacles. as a result, only the wealthiest can afford the luxury of treatment abroad. in response to these problems, the draft directive envisages the greatest possible simplification of administrative procedures, for example by reducing the obligation for prior authorisation of treatment by the national health authority, and by ensuring better exchange of information on medical services in other countries through the creation of national contact points. this is not, as some claim, about promoting 'health tourism', but about ensuring the right to a certain and high quality of care when it is needed. i also believe that in the long term the directive can help to level the playing field in healthcare across the eu. when we consider the draft directive, we must have the patient's welfare at the forefront. the role of legislators is to adopt legislation that will minimise the formalities associated with access to a doctor and allow sick citizens a wide choice of medical services. i therefore strongly support the draft directive on crossborder healthcare services and hope that the negotiations, which have been going on for seven years, will result in an agreement with the council.
in writing. − the directive on patients' rights in crossborder healthcare is an important step towards removing the barriers that patients in eu member states have faced up to now. it is primarily intended to make it easier for europeans to access healthcare in another eu member state, in particular in terms of access to services that are difficult to access in their own country. this is particularly good news for people living in border regions, especially those suffering from rare diseases and requiring specialist treatment not available in their country. i am also pleased to see a number of provisions ensuring that patients are able to accept reciprocal prescriptions, that they no longer need to take out additional insurance abroad and that they have access to medical records. the idea of setting up national focal points to inform patients of their rights is also relevant. patients should be fully informed about the procedures for accessing treatment abroad and for reimbursing the cost of such treatment (at the prices applicable in the country where the patient is insured). i believe that the solutions developed will facilitate access to safe and high quality healthcare for patients throughout the european union.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! i voted in favour of mrs grossetête's report for a number of important reasons. the directive on patients' rights in crossborder healthcare has many advantages. it removes barriers to treatment, ensures equal access to healthcare for all across the union, puts an end to discrimination against patients, introduces mutual recognition of prescriptions, reduces waiting times for doctor visits and eliminates the need for additional insurance abroad. the additional value of the directive is that it introduces broad access to medical care for people suffering from rare diseases and higher reimbursements for people with disabilities. the directive is opposed to medical tourism in that reimbursement of treatment costs will be made up to the level guaranteed in the country of insurance, if the amount is lower than the guaranteed level, only the costs actually incurred will be reimbursed. a lot of discussion has been about what's called authorization. the prior consent of the nfz will only be required for hospital treatment and expensive medical procedures. all other forms of treatment will not require prior authorisation from the nfz, provided they are covered by the so-called 'guaranteed benefits basket'. if a member state does not allow patients to receive specialised treatment at national level, the directive does not create any new right for patients to receive such treatment abroad and to receive reimbursement. an important exception is the case of people with rare diseases.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! i consider the directive on patients' rights in crossborder healthcare to be a success and that is why i voted in favour of its provisions. health is the most precious possession we have. i want europeans to have access to the highest quality medicine. the directive gives patients a chance and hope, and it forces further reforms of health care systems. the directive opens up european hospitals and clinics to polish patients, among others. it is a confirmation that europe is being built, that our priority is to improve and promote cooperation in health between eu member states.
in writing. − on 19 january 2011, the european parliament adopted a directive on patients' rights in crossborder healthcare, which aims to simplify the rules on treatment abroad. i am pleased to note that the european parliament, as a co-legislator, has played a key role in shaping clear and patient-friendly rules on, among other things, reimbursement of medical care in another country. the rules on crossborder healthcare are all the more important as they concern every citizen of the european union. the new directive guarantees the mutual recognition of prescriptions, facilitates access to information on treatment abroad, and increases treatment coverage for people with rare diseases and the possibility for disabled people to receive higher reimbursement for medical care. the european parliament is also involved in setting up national contact points in each member state to provide information on treatment abroad. these points will be in close contact with each other. finally, i would say that the directive adopted is very necessary because the current legislation on medical treatment abroad is unclear and complex, and simplifying these matters is very important from the point of view of every member of the european union.
in writing. − the directive on the application of patients' rights in crossborder healthcare is a very important document for citizens of the european union, and i have followed its development with all the more attention. i am pleased to see that the directive leaves patients the right to choose where to receive healthcare, thus strengthening the common market, which is the main theme of my work in the european parliament, and adapting to the freedom to travel and work in the countries of the european union. this health schengen will include such issues as mutual recognition of prescriptions, the end of discrimination against patients on the basis of their country of origin and the abolition of the need to have supplementary insurance abroad. another very important issue from the point of view of the common market is the issue of counterfeit medicines and medical products. the directive stresses that they are a serious problem, especially in the context of crossborder healthcare, as well as medical tourism. the directive combats this by providing for reimbursement of treatment costs up to the level guaranteed in the country of origin or, if this amount is lower than the cost of treatment/treatment, reimbursement of the costs actually incurred. the solutions put in place will help improve the situation of patients in the european union and strengthen the common market, which is why i voted in favour of the directive.
in writing. - once again, i would like to remind the european parliament of the importance of forests for the climate, water management, agriculture and culture of a country or region, especially in rural areas. however, wood products are of considerable market importance. we therefore need to be absolutely certain that timber originating in cameroon, congo or any other third country has been legally sourced, transported and marketed in compliance with the needs of the community and forest management law. the partnership with these countries will result in improved forest management, increased credibility and international competitiveness of exporting countries.
in writing. − the pacific states region is a very specific area, composed mainly of island countries, largely ethnically diverse, with a culture that is very different from that of europe and that requires different political and economic priorities. by concluding agreements with these countries, we want to allow the free movement of goods and services, which should bring commercial benefits to both sides. however, we must also ensure that we are not seen as intruders in seeking to liberalise the market, seeking to secure access to resources for ourselves, and weakening, as critics say, regional solidarity. let us make deals, open markets, promote competition, but with common sense and always for mutual benefit, helping especially regions such as the pacific area of states that often suffer from natural disasters.
in writing. − in the interests of the child, intercountry adoption should be allowed, but only if the possibilities of adoption in a member state have been exhausted. as a rule, a child should be raised in the country of which he is a citizen. foreign adoptions happen in my country, poland, too. these are usually children who, due to various illnesses, have no chance of being adopted in the country. for example, in 2006, 202 foreign families decided to take in 311 of our compatriots. 214 children from poland found italian parents, 25 french, 22 american, 20 dutch, 15 swedish, 7 german, 6 swiss, 1 belgian and 1 canadian. in western europe, the problem of orphaned children is virtually non-existent, hence the great interest in the possibility of adoption in central and eastern european countries. i believe that the european commission should first of all: 1) inform parliament of the measures that have been or will be taken at european level to protect intercountry adoption from child trafficking; 2) respond to how the commission intends to counter 'fashion' adoption. europeans are increasingly adopting children from africa because of the popularity of the practice among movie stars. however, this is neither a sufficient nor a serious basis for surrogacy.
in writing. − i welcome the results of today's vote on the draft council and commission decision on the conclusion of the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of serbia, of the other part. serbia has made significant progress in its cooperation with the european union since 2007, which has enabled the community to resume negotiations. the negotiations were concluded on 10 september 2007 and, after consultation with the eu member states, the stabilisation and association agreement was initialled in brussels on 7 november 2007. however, we must remember that full cooperation is conditional on serbia fulfilling the political condition set by the council when adopting the negotiating directives full cooperation with the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia.
in writing. - dear colleagues! one of the most effective ways to inform the public about the occurrence of dementia in older people is to raise awareness and to actively campaign for awareness. alzheimer's disease needs special attention because it is becoming a growing problem not only in the eu but also worldwide, and we know from the experts that the number is increasing all the time. we are an ageing society, we must talk about it openly, we must find solutions to the problem and above all we must stress the importance of prevention in this area, which is why i voted in favour of the report by mrs marisa matias on the european initiative on alzheimer's disease and other dementias.
in writing. − i supported the report on the european initiative on alzheimer's disease and other dementias. the issues of older people have recently been the subject of parliament's deliberations in the context of the economic crisis, labour market needs and increasing labour force participation. the dementia statistics show the magnitude of the problem. each year, 1.4 million people in europe develop dementia, and the number of people affected is estimated at 10 million. in poland, more than 200,000 people suffer from alzheimer's disease. neurodegenerative diseases are one of the main causes of disability among older people. the problem has become more acute with the increase in life expectancy. alzheimer's disease is a major economic challenge for entire societies. the world alzheimer's report, published in 2010, estimates that the global cost of alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia is $600 billion annually. a common european strategy to combat dementia is needed. we need to develop and promote prevention of alzheimer's disease, which is healthy lifestyle, physical, mental and social activity, healthy diet. carers of sick people should be provided with adequate financial and psychological support. the european alzheimer's strategy should take particular account of the needs of women, who are twice as likely to develop dementia and who are the majority of carers.
in writing. − during this plenary session we voted on the european parliament resolution on the european initiative on alzheimer's disease and other dementias. i voted for this resolution because it is a very important step towards making detailed proposals to combine existing policies and ways of dealing with these kinds of diseases. currently, neurodegenerative diseases are one of the main causes of disability among older people, and the number of people affected by these diseases is likely to increase significantly. this is all the more significant when we consider the increase in life expectancy and the decline in the proportion of people in employment to those retiring. in view of the above, it is essential to place prevention at the heart of all strategies and to focus efforts on achieving early detection. as a representative of society, i feel partly responsible for the eu's engagement in this issue.
in writing. − on 12 january, we marked the first anniversary of the tragic earthquake in haiti, which killed 222,750 people and forced some 1.7 million people to flee their homes. in the wake of these tragic events, the european parliament adopted a resolution on 19 january describing the situation on the island one year after the disaster. despite the efforts of numerous international organisations and international aid to rebuild the country, the situation in haiti remains volatile and the country is in crisis. ten months after the earthquake, the island has been battling a cholera epidemic, and the validity of presidential and parliamentary elections is being questioned by international observers. parliament called on the eu and the international community to show solidarity with the island and to cooperate more closely with the haitian authorities, given the current situation in the country, and stressed that any reconstruction measures should be taken in consultation with the people of the country. the european parliament also stresses the importance of the form in which aid to haiti should be provided, namely in the form of donations and not in the form of loans, which would lead to debt. finally, i would like to express my solidarity with haiti and hope that the reconstruction work in the country will be speeded up.

based on religion or belief – which was adopted by consensus in december 2010. we make a concerted effort every year to build on that consensus, so that the international community can send a firm and united message. we are considering another initiative to rally strong cross-regional support on this theme at the forthcoming session of the un human rights council in march. we also raise the issue of freedom of religion or belief during our human rights dialogues and urge countries to eradicate discrimination and intolerance. our delegations closely monitor these issues around the world, and the european union’s next annual human rights report this spring will address the situation of religious minorities around the world. honourable members, i am fully committed to keeping freedom of religion or belief at the top of our agenda. the next foreign affairs council on 31 january will again address this issue so that the european union can step up its efforts to promote religious freedom.

vice-president of the commission/ high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, the events which followed the elections in belarus on 19 december have come as a shock to all of us: the force used by the authorities against their citizens prompted statements of concern and condemnation across the world. my colleagues and i have met with many of those affected, among the opposition movement, civil society, the families of those imprisoned and the population at large. we have had the opportunity to express our sympathy and solidarity and to listen. however, honourable members, the time has come to act. i greatly appreciate the fact that members of this parliament have already been able to contribute to our reflections on this issue and that my colleague, commissioner füle, was able to present our current thinking to the afet committee last week. i am looking forward to studying the eu resolution which emerges from your debates. it is important for all of us to be as focused as possible in our thinking, given the urgency of the situation that we are addressing. i have spent time with a number of representatives of the opposition and the wider public in belarus, including, as i have mentioned, relatives of those detained. i have also met foreign minister martynov. these conversations have left me in no doubt that the events we witnessed were an affront to our vision of respect for human rights, fundamental freedoms and democracy. not only was there unwarranted use of force, but the electoral process as a whole was also clearly undermined by the detention of civil society and opposition representatives. the assessment by the osce-odihr supports this conclusion. many of those detained in the last few weeks have been released. however, a significant group – as many as 30 people – still face charges that could lead to very substantial prison sentences and, as honourable members know, that group includes some presidential candidates. mr president, i have already condemned the repressive measures taken by the authorities in minsk and i have called for the immediate release of all those detained on political grounds, as well as the reopening of the osce office in minsk. i have reinforced this message in a joint statement with us secretary of state hillary clinton. in my meeting with foreign minister martynov, i emphasised that the eu expects an immediate response from the belarusian authorities to the demands of the international community. in determining the next steps we take, we need to start from basic principles. the first of these principles is that the security and safety of peaceful activists, including presidential candidates, must be at the forefront of our minds at all times. the second is that belarusians are our neighbours and partners, and their interests should be paramount. while we express our concern to the authorities, we cannot isolate the people. the third principle is that respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms is at the core of eu foreign policy and of the eastern partnership and is part of a set of common values which we share with our closest partners. we will work with those partners, as we have done with the united states, to maximise the strength of the message sent to belarus by the international community. mr president, our assessment leads to a clear conclusion: that we should use our channels to convey a firm and prompt reaction. that reaction should give the authorities in belarus a clear signal of our views, without isolating citizens and civil society. our reaction should be a balanced one. on the one hand, we have to consider targeted measures against the belarusian authorities and, i believe, to conduct a review of sanctions. on the other hand, we need to have an intensified dialogue with, and to support, civil society and citizens – and in practical terms that means continuing our assistance to ngos, the media and students, and perhaps an increased effort to enhance mobility for citizens who wish to travel to the european union. in the short term, reintroducing a travel ban for president lukashenko, and extending that ban to further named individuals, is certainly an option if detainees are not released. with regard to intensified support for civil society, i have asked the external action service, in cooperation with the commission, to prepare options for urgent measures focusing on ngos, media and students. i know that the european parliament has scope to provide scholarships for students expelled from university and i hope, mr president, that this facility can be exploited. of course we shall be trying to leverage additional resources from elsewhere, including member states. i mentioned earlier the issue of mobility and i am thinking in particular of visa facilitation: i want to encourage member states’ consulates in minsk to facilitate the delivery of visas as an ad hoc measure in the interests of belarusian citizens. mr president, the short-term measures i have just described will, of course, have to be considered by the foreign affairs council on 31 january but it is not too early to reflect on some longer-term aspects of our relations with belarus. firstly, i said earlier that we need to work with other international partners on this issue and that is one reason why belarus should continue to participate in the multilateral track that we have available, and why we need to engage strongly with our eastern partnership countries to build a consensus on this issue. secondly, as far as bilateral financial assistance from the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument (enpi) is concerned, we should place a stronger focus on the needs of the population and on civil society. finally, last year we drew up a joint interim plan, mapping out the development of our relations with belarus in the medium term. i believe we need to pause in this process. that does not mean abandoning the joint interim plan, but we need further consultation, including with civil society, and a review if necessary. mr president, this is the framework within which we are currently working. i am now very interested to hear the views of members of parliament.

the next item on the agenda is the statement by the president on the eu recognition of the genocide of the roma during the second world war (2010/3020 ((rsp)). roma are now the largest ethnic minority in the european union. they are also the most oppressed community in europe today. during world war ii, they were racially persecuted by the nazis, as were the jews. hundreds of thousands of roma, citizens of europe for generations, have been murdered. the 66th anniversary of the liberation of auschwitz-birkenau, which we celebrated on 27 january, reminds us that roma were the third largest group of victims of the camp. unfortunately, this fact is not widely known to europeans. only some eu member states have officially recognised the genocide of the roma. it is time to make europeans aware that the roma living among us have been traumatized by the genocide as a community. education is the best way to fight discrimination. the european parliament is the voice of the union in the fight for human rights. today we remember our roma brothers and sisters. we want to remember their suffering and to understand their situation better. colleagues, there will now be a very short discussion on this topic so please do not leave the chamber. first we will have a statement from the council and, as you know, roma integration is one of the priorities of the hungarian presidency. this will be followed by a statement from the vice-president of the commission and then short statements on behalf of the political groups.

in writing. ladies and gentlemen, the victims of the tyranny of the third reich during world war ii is still a very delicate subject, but one worth exploring. today we want to broaden the context of the concept of the holocaust, which functions in the public consciousness as the mass extermination of the jews. the purges of the elderly ethnic, national and social groups during the second world war are also worthy of remembrance and commemoration. knowledge of this subject is not widespread enough, especially among young europeans. that is why we are trying to bring up in today's debate the painful and somewhat forgotten issue of the extermination of the roma. the porajmos, as the term is used for the genocide of the roma population, took between 500,000 and 2 million roma from all over europe. in auschwitz, they were the third nation after the jews and the poles in terms of murders committed. these facts leave no doubt about the enormous losses suffered by the roma, which places us as europeans under an obligation to promote and commemorate this unjust victim of genocide. raising awareness is a priority for current and future generations.

mr. chairman, please! we are very pleased that the referendum in south sudan has gone so smoothly. our observers have consistently praised the progress of the observation mission. the evaluation of the referendum itself in terms of the standards we promote is also positive. the referendum was credible, well organised and gave the voters a chance to express their will. it was also clear how much the sudanese people were attached to this referendum, as the turnout reached 60% on the fourth day. this clearly shows the degree of determination in the matter of self-determination. president bashir has often been criticised by our parliament, but this time we must appreciate the statement he made on 24 january in juba, which mrs ashton mentioned. the president has said that he will accept any decision that comes out of the referendum, even one that means the secession of south sudan, and the will of the people - as all indications suggest - is very clear. i also share the wishes and hope that if the two parts of sudan are indeed divided, they will enjoy peaceful coexistence. now it's important that this calm atmosphere of the referendum be complemented by a calm period of the announcement of the results and the transformation of the two countries. many observers fear that the current wave of unrest and democratization expectations in several countries, which has also reached sudan, could become a pretext to freeze the peace process and prevent the completion of ambitious plans. on the other hand, there are positive signs, for example from the african union, which is known to be ready to recognize the independence of the new african state. we must also be aware that the referendum is not the end of the matter, that the ultimate success will be the implementation of the will of the people of sudan. as we know, this could happen on july 9th, when sudan's independence is proclaimed and we can then rejoice in the end of this bloody conflict.
