in writing. − i am convinced that action to promote the use of egnos and galileo in civil aviation is crucial to the creation of a single european air traffic management system. unfortunately, as the rapporteur has pointed out in her document, the introduction of galileo is facing new problems. i agree with the commission's call for rapid egnos certification for civil aviation. i have already stressed on many occasions that i am enthusiastic about the concept of the single european sky and the sesar single air traffic management system. the rapid and full realisation of european airspace is a very important strategic step towards the real integration of the community and the strengthening of the common market. without galileo there will be no sesar and without it there will be no single european sky 2. and let's remember that this area in particular is a system of connected vessels. the weakness of one element will have a fatal effect on the others.
in writing. - i welcome the outcome of today's vote, especially as i was the rapporteur member for the document on the eu-us aviation agreement. it was a document of particular importance. the european union and the united states together account for approximately 60% of the world's air traffic. the future opening of the market to eu and us airlines on a non-discriminatory basis will offer better services to passengers and carriers in air transport, bring significant economic benefits and create jobs. unfortunately, the european parliament was not involved in the negotiations of the community-us agreement and ultimately had no influence on the content of this document. this is an unacceptable situation. i therefore agree with the main point of the report adopted today by mr simpson on international air traffic agreements: the european parliament should be involved in the negotiations from the outset or at least kept informed of their progress.
in writing. - i would like to express my full support for the directive on the charging of road tolls to heavy goods vehicles. i would particularly like to support a provision which is very important for the european environment. i hope that the lower charges for less polluting cars will motivate the remaining owners of transport companies to upgrade their fleet. crops located in the vicinity of frequented roads would also be much less exposed to exhaust pollution. i also see the increase in the traffic charges during rush hour as a positive aspect. these restrictions will improve road safety and driving comfort for all road users. this restriction will also improve the infrastructure, which is most damaged during peak hours.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? i voted for the euro-vignette because i believe that solutions of this kind are capable of ensuring full harmonisation of the european charging system for heavy goods vehicles, thus facilitating efficient transit through the member states, avoiding unnecessary delays. in my view, the introduction of the 'polluter pays' principle will reduce pollution and noise caused by heavy goods vehicles not equipped with euro v and vi engines which are not subject to road tolls. in addition, the principle that member states will be able to determine the use of the revenue from the charges collected, but that at least 15% of the revenue should go to financial support for ten-t projects, will ensure that transport is more sustainable.
in writing. i voted for the directive. i believe that the decision to extend the scope of the eurovignette to cover external costs, i.e. the costs of environmental pollution and noise, is more favourable than the previous decision, which was limited to covering road infrastructure costs. this directive is favourable to transit countries, so polish meps should be particularly concerned about it. it is also worth noting that the lower the environmental category of the truck, the lower the charges are to be. fortunately, vehicles with a payload of between 3.5 and 12 tonnes and passenger car users will be exempt from the charges. the fares will be structured according to the time of day, which i think will help discourage the use of sections at risk of traffic jams during peak hours. an important principle of the directive is also the provision on the expenditure of revenue from customs duties. they are to be reinvested in transport infrastructure, without reservation as to type, with a minimum of 15% of the proceeds to be allocated to ten-t (trans european transport networks) projects. i believe that we also need long-term action to bring the methods of calculating external costs into line in all member states. this could ensure transparency of communications for the european road transport industry.

member of the commission. − mr president, i welcome on behalf of the commission the report submitted by the sure committee. this is a real contribution to the preparations for the next financial duplication of national budgets, but about delivering common goals beyond the capacity of nation states where european funds can realise economies of scale or create synergies. in short, the european budget should be used where it makes a difference, as it has the nature of an investment and has no deficit. we also share a vision of the so-called ‘traditional’ policies – namely the common mr president, i would like to say a few words on the need to move towards own resources reform. i believe that the dominating role of gni-based revenue makes a decision on the eu budget over-politicised and less efficiency-oriented. it facilitates demands to freeze or to reduce eu spending. it leads to the logic expressed in the context of the 2011 budget negotiations that if we cut our national budgets due to the crisis, we should apply the same approach to the eu budget. it is, however, not at all obvious that with an additional own resource that would reduce the dependence on gni we can expect a revolution in eu capacities to finance growth and structural change. there is always a risk that the same coalition that adopts the budgetary decision in the council can also adopt the same decision in the european parliament. if we care for europe, we should move away from responding to the expectations of finance ministers and move towards citizens’ expectations. the success of a national politician returning home from brussels negotiations should not be based on the message that the government will pay less to the eu budget but, for example, on the message that the eu will help to make small companies fund innovation projects. it is clear that the way eu costs are financed should be fully transparent. this could be easier to achieve with only one tax, but it is also feasible to build the revenue on a group of taxes that meet criteria on transparency, equity, visibility, efficiency and sufficient harmonisation.

in writing. while the freezing of eu spending was justified during the economic crisis, today, when we think about the multiannual financial framework, we cannot use the arguments of two years ago. we must ask ourselves how the union will function in the next seven years: will it be a union of solidarity, one that delivers on its commitments and builds an innovative economy and a common foreign policy in line with the lisbon treaty? or the union, which has ambitious goals in the treaty but which everyone knows is a sham? i strongly support this first model and support the rapporteur's view that the next mff should be increased by 5% compared to the 2013 level. such a change will bring us closer to the ambitious treaty targets, and a mere 5% increase in spending is de facto a minimal increase in spending, as the inflation rate is currently 3.2%. moreover, this small increase in the eu budget benefits the poorest regions, which are the biggest beneficiaries of eu aid to make up for development gaps. i hope that the next polish presidency will make it a priority to reconcile the positions of the so-called net contributors: germany, france and the united kingdom, with the position of parliament expressed in the ambitious report by mr garriga polledo.
in writing. the new multiannual financial framework is very important. why would you do that? the future of the european union will depend to a large extent on them. the debate on the financial perspective is not easy, as many member states are feeling the effects of the economic crisis. the reluctance to increase the eu budget is understandable. however, financial sceptics should be aware of the benefits that the single market brings to the economies of individual member states. european integration has a positive and stimulating effect on the economy. the european parliament also wants the new financial framework to be structured in such a way as to increase competitiveness and promote social inclusion. the eu budget funds tasks that are of vital importance to the citizens of all member states. it's not an abstraction. cohesion policy and the common agricultural policy affect the daily lives of millions of citizens. there is no doubt that some of the eu's tasks could not be fulfilled from other sources. increasing social, economic and infrastructural cohesion and equalizing opportunities in the agricultural sector are objectives worth supporting. it's worth spending european money on. the european union cannot do more in more member states with less budget. it's not possible. that's why we need a bigger and more ambitious budget.

in writing. the poorest regions of the european union are now developing rapidly, thanks in part to european funds. although many new roads are being built or repaired and internet networks are being installed, there is still a great deal of need because the distance to the most developed regions is very long. when we joined the european union, there were concerns that poland and the new member states would not take full advantage of the opportunities offered by membership and that european funds would be spent in a reckless manner. there were also concerns about corruption, because opportunity - that is, big money - makes a thief. however, analyses show that european money is well spent in poland and is not subject to unfair practices. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council at the next meeting of the european council in brussels on 21 and 22 june. even if the european parliament votes to increase the european budget, which i hope it will, it is important now to convince individual countries that it is worth supporting the political position of the parliament.
in writing. i would like to congratulate mr salvador garridze on the comprehensive report and the impressive work on the compromise amendments. i agree with the rapporteur that cohesion policy, which has proved its worth, should find its proper place in the new multiannual financial framework. however, better coordination and complementarity between the different funds and simplification of procedures should be pursued. changes to the control and management systems of the funds, which are intended to increase the effectiveness of their interventions, should be based on a thorough analysis of their current functioning. i also support the view that unused appropriations should remain in the cohesion budget and not go back to the member states. i also believe that a careful analysis of the possible implications of the inclusion of the european development fund in the union budget is necessary, especially in the light of the eu's commitments towards third countries.
in writing. the creation of the so-called transition regions proposed in the report means that the relatively rich areas of the poorer member states will continue to receive support and will be able to gradually prepare themselves for the total loss of these additional funds. for the main beneficiaries of cohesion policy, who must think long term, considering the possibility of such a group of regions is certainly a very positive solution. if parliament were to adopt such a proposal today, it would be a very important voice in the debate on the future shape of cohesion policy.
in writing. the report by mr garriga polledo focuses on the union 2020 programme. i believe that the conversion of large amounts of money to this programme could lead to a reduction in the funding of programmes important for cohesion and european development, such as the cohesion fund. the results show that the fund is by far the most effective instrument for achieving the objectives of the treaty on european union and the treaty of lisbon. it is therefore important that its resources be increased. many european countries have been hit hard by the economic crisis, and the cohesion fund is now a lever for them to actively combat unemployment and to boost the regions. on the other hand, it is important that the union financially supports energy projects and innovation. these two investment divisions are key to the rapid development of the european community. two thirds of energy raw materials are currently imported from countries outside the union, mainly from russia. this means a significant outflow of capital beyond our borders, and we should therefore allocate more resources to support infrastructure investments that allow for the diversification of supply and thus lower their price, including the most important element of diversification, the nabucco pipeline. the report also lacks clear guidance on support for shale gas exploration in the coming years. the union must not forget that by investing wisely in energy today, it saves capital tomorrow.
i would like to make it clear that the recommendations adopted by parliament today are not so clear-cut in polish circumstances. these recommendations will lead to higher transport costs and will clearly be at a disadvantage to carriers with older transport. the positive side is that additional resources will be created that can be invested in sustainable transport, in particular the opportunity to develop high-speed rail and waterways. but i want to subscribe to the statements of those colleagues who say that there are not only positive things here. these recommendations will also cause a whole series of complications for a very large number of carriers in my country.
i voted against the audy report. i cannot accept a document that blocks the indect project. i do not agree with the statement that the project being carried out at the famous krakow university, the academy of mining and metallurgy, is contrary to the charter of fundamental rights. the aim of his research is to implement resolutions on combating paedophilia, the sale of arms via the internet, the fight against drug trafficking and human trafficking, which are topics we have discussed many times in this chamber. this is an innovative project that perfectly fills the gaps in the security systems of the eu member states, especially at the internet level. he's targeting lawbreakers, and they're the ones who might be most afraid of his assumptions. moreover, it is a good basis for building an integrated security network to defend against cyber attacks. russia has these solutions, the united states has them, china has them, and for some years now we have not been able to see them at the level of the european union. so i don't understand why the funding for the whole project has been withheld, especially since it's the only project that was treated like this in the report of mr. audy.
although the european parliament has repeatedly recognised the benefits to the internal market of an improved contract law framework, the introduction of a new contract law system through an optional instrument faces a number of serious problems, both substantive and procedural. first of all, the proposals presented reflect the commission's position, which is not supported by a substantive public debate. we therefore do not know the positions of individual member states, including representatives of business and consumer circles. as some of the proposed documents on which case law will be based appear to be unclear, this may lead to divergent legal interpretations. finally, the introduction of an optional instrument would have a significant economic impact on businesses and consumers. the costs of the required training, the exchange of standard contract forms and possible legal proceedings can be very high. it seems unreasonable to impose additional financial burdens on companies in these difficult economic times. on the basis of the above, i voted to reject the report.
the economic crisis, demographic problems and rising unemployment are all having a major impact on the budgetary constraints of the member states. a european budget with long-term planning capabilities should therefore be an instrument to support the development of national economies. the europe 2020 strategy, which encourages job creation and social inclusion, seems to be an important element in helping to overcome the crisis. in this respect, it is particularly important that small and medium-sized enterprises are also covered. i therefore agree with the demand for greater support for all programmes and instruments to support these enterprises, including programmes for competitiveness, innovation and the use of the structural funds. the greatest challenge for the european union will be to maintain its competitiveness, boost growth and combat unemployment. i therefore stress the urgent need to promote growth through investment in the knowledge-based economy. strengthening the link between education, research and employment will foster integration, mobility and specialisation.

in writing. - article 27 of this report contains information which is not true. the statement that indect constantly monitors the internet and personal computers is not true, as confirmed by the ethical review that indect underwent on 15 march 2011 in brussels, with the participation of experts from austria, france, the netherlands, germany and the united kingdom. the ethical audit was positive for indect and no deficiencies related to the ethical aspects of the project were found. indect has been continuously monitored by the european commission since its inception. the commission has not found any deficiencies so far. moreover, this item does not fit into the report as a whole and is specifically targeted at the indect project, leaving out other similar projects that are financed by european union funds. the main objective of the indect (english: intelligent information system supporting observation, searching and detection for security of citizens in urban environment) project, conducted by the academy of mining and metallurgy in kraków, is to develop research on information technologies that increase the security of residents of urbanized areas. indect is designed to detect threats through monitoring, including in particular pornography, arms, drugs or human organ trafficking, as well as to protect data and privacy.

i expect, commissioner, that the summit will be about modernization. i would just like to remind you that the modernization of russia is not only economic issues, not only energy issues, but also political modernization, the relationship between the government and the people. i'm asking you to take up the matter. it's also russia's relations with its neighbors and with its so-called sphere of influence. i would like to say very clearly that the agreement between the european union and ukraine, the association agreement, is also beneficial for russia and that we are watching with great concern the very strong political pressure on ukraine on the eve of the conclusion of the negotiations, in the last phase of these negotiations. we ask you to make that very clear to the russian side. these are very important elements of mutual trust between the institutions of the european union and the member states and russia.
the eu-russia summit will probably cover a wide range of issues, but one of the most important is probably energy security. russia has been conducting an extremely intense campaign for several months to exclude its gas infrastructure from the rules of the third energy package, from the rules of our antitrust law, which prohibits simultaneous, parallel control of the raw material and the transmission network. we have visits to brussels by minister szmatko, president kramer of south stream and president miller of gazprom. this is a big campaign. russia needs to hear the very clear position of the european union on this issue, that we are not going to apply a preferential tariff to russia, that we want the central european gas market to be more competitive, to be more demonopolised. commissioner, can you tell us clearly whether the european commission is prepared to make such declarations at the summit?
before the upcoming summit, we can indeed say that the european union lacks a single and coherent strategy towards russia, and the current pragmatic cooperation based on a strategy of small steps can very easily be broken at the first better crisis, as happened in 2008 during the war with georgia or after the cutting off of gas supplies in 2009. in the context of this latest event, it is very important to emphasise the meaning of the word 'diversification', which in europe is often synonymous with the construction of a large number of different gas pipelines from russia. the construction of the south and nord stream pipelines is considered as diversification. the eu should, however, focus on securing gas supplies from sources other than russia: promoting the nabucco pipeline from azerbaijan more, investing in gas ports and shale gas exploration. it is also very important to continue to put pressure on the russian authorities at various levels to improve the human rights situation in russia. in addition to the eu-russia summit discussions, the twice-yearly consultations involving representatives of the european union and diplomats from the russian ministry of foreign affairs should be strongly strengthened.
i think the russian authorities should hear that we expect them to be held accountable. russia can be a very important partner for the european union, for example, in resolving some of the unresolved, frozen conflicts in europe. i think the russian authorities should hear that while vegetables and gas are important, they should stop supporting the separatists in transnistria, that we expect russia to stop supplying arms to azerbaijan and armenia because it is very dangerous for the future of the region, and that we also expect russia to fulfill its obligations under the 2008 agreement that concerns georgia. we expect the withdrawal of russian troops from abkhazia and south ossetia, we expect russia to respect georgia's right to think and decide its own future.

the european union is in talks with russia about the energy future, but a new group is now being set up, from what i understand, to discuss the third energy package in the context of gas security. and i would ask you, commissioner, and commissioner oettinger to keep the european parliament informed of the progress of the talks and the outcome of the negotiations of this group. we'd also like to know who's gonna be on the negotiating team. i was told by one of the representatives of the russian energy company that they, as a company, would be involved in these negotiations. i'd like to know if that's true and if representatives of big companies will be involved in the negotiations on the russian side. it is also very important to the european parliament that competition law in the energy sector is respected without any exceptions. during the recent presentations of the south stream investment plans in brussels, it was clear that russia and gazprom wanted privileges and special status. we can't agree to that.
nuclear safety issues both in the member states and in those neighbouring the community should be the subject of particular attention by the european union. following the fukushima nuclear power plant accident in japan, the commission announced endurance tests for eu power plants. it's a very good sign and a very good decision. we're waiting for it to be implemented. in view of the safety of all europeans, particular attention should be paid to the appropriate use of all available means to raise safety standards and eliminate potential risks from nuclear energy. power stations located not only in the member states but also in countries bordering the community are potentially at risk. the union's member states should also be given the necessary incentives and support to carry out reliable endurance tests of union power plants. i would also like to stress the profound need to invest in both nuclear research and other important research to anticipate and prevent accidents and their negative consequences in the future.
following the fukushima disaster, public concern about the safety of nuclear power plants in europe has increased. it's understandable, you know. the reports coming in from japan are sometimes frightening, they are terrifying, they indicate a huge contamination of the land. none of us would want a repeat of this in europe any more than we would want a repeat of chernobyl. but all the more so to allay public fears everything must be done to guarantee the safety of nuclear energy in europe. that's why stress tests are so important. but it is also important that they be of a high standard, that they guarantee objectivity, that they give certainty and credibility that their implementation is based on the anticipation of emergencies, crisis situations, which may happen in europe as they did in japan. we must do everything we can to restore security and confidence in this energy source in europe. however, other energy sources, such as unconventional shale gas, must also be considered.
for many years, nuclear power was considered the energy of the future: green, efficient, zero-emission. the chernobyl and more recently the fukushima disasters have shown the other side of the coin. but today we cannot, as the left would like, have the task of carrying out 'stress tests' in order to find a pretext for abandoning the atomic bomb in europe by interpreting the results in a biased way. today, our aim must be to improve the safety of nuclear power stations, to reassure the public and to change the negative image of nuclear energy in europe. that should be our priority today. that is why i do not understand the voices of the left who are talking about another tax on nuclear energy and the final abandonment of this type of energy source. this path, in the absence of alternative sources, will lead to skyrocketing electricity prices. today, europe needs to revise nuclear law in terms of the competences of the member states, to establish common standards and to optimise safety standards in the union. the 'stress tests' must provide a response to the security situation, taking into account all possible forms of threats from terrorist attacks to power cuts.

in writing. the economies of some eu member states, including my own poland are already feeling the damaging effects of the arbitrarily imposed climate and energy package as a tool to achieve the 3x20 political objective. but this policy goal is often distorted, too, because they talk about reducing energy consumption by 20 percent, and they talk about increasing efficiency by 20 percent, and that's not the same thing. the frequent misuse of the term 'efficiency' in eu documents is due to a misunderstanding of the concept of 'energy efficiency' and how it is assessed, i.e. whether it is 'gross national efficiency', 'per capita efficiency' or 'conversion efficiency', e.g. primary energy into useful work. emphasising efficiency gains rather than consumption reductions will create a favourable focus on innovative technologies. and this is the biggest potential reduction in emissions - even greater than the 20% declared. member states should be free to choose the way and timetable for reducing emissions, mainly through efficiency gains. in the case of poland, the main concerns are the great potential it offers: 1. mass thermal modernisation of new and old buildings and 2. extensive replacement of old district heating plants by modern electricity-generating plants. the climate and energy package needs to be revised to better align member states to reduce emissions.

president-in-office of the council. − mr president, honourable members, i would like to read out the council’s political statement on the transparency register. ‘the council considers transparency as a principle of paramount importance for the european union. the treaties provide that, in order to promote good governance and ensure the participation of civil society, the union’s institutions, bodies, offices and agencies shall conduct their work as openly as possible and that decisions shall be taken as openly and as closely as possible to the citizens.‘ in line with these provisions, the council remains committed to giving the fullest possible effect to the principle of transparency. it also recognises that citizens expect that those who act on their behalf at the eu level respect the highest possible standards.‘ the council therefore welcomes and supports the initiative undertaken by the european parliament and the commission to establish a joint “transparency register”.‘ the council considers that transparency should guide relations with interest representatives and that the register provides a useful basis on which to build and interact with them in an open, inclusive and consistent fashion.‘ the council has received the invitation of the european parliament and the commission to join the register. the council is ready to consider having a role in the register and looks forward to discuss the possible modalities with the two other institutions.’

in writing. - i voted in favour of the agreement because it is mutually beneficial to the parties' interests in the fisheries sector. the seychelles fishing authority, which has an effective vessel monitoring system, is of great importance for this cooperation. this is particularly important in the light of the problem of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing faced by the authorities in this area. the agreement covers a number of issues, including the presence of observers during fishing. european vessels authorised to fish in seychelles' waters shall take on board observers appointed by the seychelles authorities and each tuna seiner shall take on board for the duration of the voyage at least two seychelles seamen, in agreement with the shipowner, from a list of names provided by the competent authority of seychelles. the arrangements cover not only strictly pragmatic aspects but also a multiannual sectoral programme which envisages cooperation in the framework of responsible fishing, sustainable fisheries and joint scientific research. the most important effect of the agreement is the creation of 230 jobs at sea for the seychelles, 2900 jobs in the seychelles and 760 derived jobs in europe in related industries, which will undoubtedly contribute to the economic recovery of the sector.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? canada is one of the world's leading producers of aircraft and aviation equipment. at present, only six member states have bilateral agreements on air service certification. the proposed agreement on civil aviation security, like the agreement with the usa, will significantly improve cooperation between the community and canada and regulate this issue in all eu countries. the agreement will allow for the standardisation of certification schemes. it will reduce the duplication of tests and checks by building on mutual trust in these systems and comparing differences. at the same time, it will launch joint inspections, studies and the exchange of safety data. mutual recognition of certification arrangements will bring significant savings to the operations of european and canadian airlines. the agreement will therefore improve the competitiveness of aviation markets on the one hand, and their safety on the other, by bringing regulators closer together. on the basis of the foregoing, i hereby consent to the conclusion of the contract.
in writing. - i voted in favour because the current cohesion policy, despite the difficulties with the use of the cohesion funds, must be consistently continued because of its far-reaching objective. the cohesion of the union is the efficient use of the potential of economically backward regions and growth with economies of scale throughout the union. this is why the focus is on transport infrastructure projects that facilitate the functioning of the common market and on the environment. in the new financial perspective, the funds cannot be dispersed over sectoral projects. there is also a need to improve coherence within member states and to better use financial resources for climate change-related infrastructure investments, such as hydro-technical structures. in poland, for example, the cohesion funds are poorly used for public transport railways, trams, internet. attention should be paid to more efficient use of resources through recycling. a too small percentage of eu funds is also allocated to heat-upgrading, especially in the countries of central and eastern europe. it is in the union's interest that the division between the major centres and the backward peripheries should disappear, so that they are not merely a market and a reservoir of labour.
in writing. − the implementation of cohesion policy in the period 2007-2013 deserves the attention of parliament for several important reasons, namely: the systematic increase in cohesion is strategically important for the future of the community; the cohesion fund is an opportunity for new member states and regions with particularly difficult development conditions; the committee on budgetary control has raised reservations about the implementation of the policy in recent years because of the excessive error rate. the report by mr mikolasik deserves our support.
in writing. − european crossborder cooperation is now one of the pillars of cohesion policy. on the one hand, it contributes to the creation of transnational projects and eu strategies, and on the other, it contributes to the reduction of barriers between territories and regions. i am convinced that effective territorial cooperation is important not only within the community but above all in the border areas with the member states of the european union. moreover, during the polish presidency of the council of the eu, we will have the opportunity to promote harmonized rules for the implementation of crossborder cooperation programmes at the eu's internal and external borders. in this context, i consider the report by maria teresa sanchez schmid on the challenges for territorial cooperation the future timetable for crossborder, transnational and interregional cooperation to be an important contribution to regional policy and i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the current situation and future synergies for greater effectiveness of the erdf and other structural funds. a study carried out in poland to identify barriers to the use of the structural funds shows that the two main obstacles are the lack of systematic information and the bureaucratic system of applying and settling eu funds. in particular, i would like to draw attention to the simplification of the application procedure for funding, both at national and regional level. this is a priority for the efficient use of all funds. i also call on the commission to simplify the concept of cohesion policy and to focus it on results rather than on complicated control procedures. the new policy must be characterised by greater flexibility, proportionality and transparency in the use of funds. the simplification of procedures would be facilitated by the harmonisation of the rules on management, eligibility, audit and reporting for projects financed by the erdf, the esf, the cohesion fund, the eafrd and the european fisheries fund. greater coordination of assistance from different funds will improve the effective handling of complex problems. for example, the problem of unemployment requires both training for the unemployed, promotion of entrepreneurship and support for structural infrastructure. there are different funds that apply here. only by working together effectively will they reduce unemployment. such a systematic approach can also improve access to the necessary information for potential beneficiaries.
in writing. − as the last year has shown, the so-called stability and growth pact, which is intended to effectively deter member states from breaking the macroeconomic assumptions of the euro area, has not worked very effectively, broadly speaking. this was largely because member states felt impunity, as the penalties provided for in the system were not automatic. the main thrust of the proposed solutions is stronger coordination of the financial policies of individual member states and more severe and automatic sanctions to force them to exercise greater macroeconomic discipline.
in writing. − consumer rights require constant attention, both in the area of legal regulation: the scope of regulation, the subject of regulation, the obligations and rights of the parties, and in the area of compliance with the law. it is good that we periodically review and make adjustments. information for consumers, the media for this information, goods with reduced value, the possibility of returning goods are particularly important issues today. these key issues and principles are reflected in the report by mr schwaba.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? in today's vote i supported the amendments to the consumer rights directive to make it easier to shop online, because it is a very important step towards completely removing barriers to the flow of goods while safeguarding consumers' rights. the guaranteed right to reliable information on the possibility of withdrawal, the price of the product, the cost of the consignment and the total purchase price and the trader's data will be aimed at increasing the security of trade and will also be a sales incentive. consumers very often complain that their right to enjoy all the benefits of the common market is not complete, which is reflected in a lack of trust in online transactions and a sense of legal uncertainty about the extent of the protection consumers should be surrounded by. the reason for the reluctance of entrepreneurs to enter into foreign transactions is the differences in the legal regulations in the various member states. for this reason, a legal solution at community level is necessary. experts estimate that up to a quarter of all trade will move online by 2015, so it is very important that trust in this type of transaction is increased. i would like to congratulate the author of this report and all those involved in the project.
in writing. - the increasingly popular online shopping has the potential to become simpler and safer with this directive. this is good news for the polish presidency, because e-commerce is one of our priorities, through which we want to increase the competitiveness of the eu economy. once the new rules come into force, the seller will be required to provide clear information on the countries to which he sends his consignments. many shops today do not ship to all eu countries, and our business is often interrupted.
in writing. − as the permanent rapporteur on the legal basis in the legal affairs committee of the european parliament, i would like to draw attention to one aspect of the report, namely the question of the legal basis. given the controversy surrounding nuclear energy today and the fact that the eu's institutional system has changed since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, i believe that the european parliament should be involved in the decision-making process in the field of nuclear energy. that is why i have recommended article 192 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and articles 31 and 32 of the euratom treaty as the appropriate legal basis for this directive. unfortunately, due to changes in the timetable of the legal affairs committee, my opinion was not taken into account by the itre committee responsible, which voted by a minimal majority to accept the euratom treaty as the sole legal basis. i believe that this has been to the detriment of the transparency of the decision-making process on a matter as important to eu citizens as nuclear energy.
in writing. − economic growth and societal development depend to a large extent on the health of citizens. the quality of the products we eat and the way they are produced are essential to our well-being, which is why the health of european union citizens should be an important aspect of our agricultural policy. by introducing a more conscious cap, we will be able to combat more effectively the diseases of civilisation linked to unhealthy lifestyles and poor nutrition. obesity, diabetes, cancer, and various diseases of the blood system are real threats to citizens. statistics show that cardiovascular disease causes about 4.3 million deaths in europe each year, and more than 1.7 million people die of cancer. i think this report is going in the wrong direction, which is why i voted against the report 'the cap to 2020: meeting the challenges of the future in terms of food, natural resources and territorial aspects'.
in writing. − polish meps voted today against a resolution on the common agricultural policy after 2013. the proposals contained in the parliamentary resolution are, in our opinion, conservative and may harm the competitiveness of both polish and european agriculture.
in writing. - i declare that i voted against the report by albert dessa. although the report contains many good ideas, it is bad for european agriculture because it does not support the idea of full equalization of direct subsidies, it perpetuates discrimination against new member states and it maintains the absurd situation that in agriculture rich countries are helped more and poor countries less. i could not vote for the report because of its contents.

we have received news of the death of otto von habsburg. otto von habsburg-lothringen was one of the first promoters of european integration and co-creator of the idea of paneurope. for many years he was the chairman of the international pan-european union, the oldest european integration movement. for two decades, as a member of the european people's party group, he was also a great promoter of the enlargement of the european union to include the countries of central europe. our former colleague from the european parliament has left us. on 25 june another of our colleagues, jan kułakowski, former mep from the alde group, also died. as a polish emigrant, he served as secretary-general of the world labour organization for 14 years, even during the communist regime in poland. in the government i led, he was the chief negotiator for the eu membership for four years. jan kułakowski has made a great contribution to poland's ability to lead the work of the council of the union today. ladies and gentlemen, we have lost two outstanding europeans with very different backgrounds. their lives were linked by the idea of a peaceful reintegration of our entire continent. they're gone, but they've left their legacy to future generations, including us in this room. the way europe has changed in their lifetime is proof of how much can be done even when the starting point is crisis and difficulty. we will not forget their contribution to the european idea. we'll continue their achievements. the next item is the report by werner langen, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on otc derivatives, central counterparties and trade repositories (com(2010)0484 – c7-0265/2010 – 2010/0250(cod)) (a7-0223/2011).
mr. chairman, please! it is a great pleasure to have you here today to address a difficult but important issue. the rapporteur rightly noted that, in addition to combating the consequences of the recession, measures should be taken to introduce the appropriate regulations to remedy its causes. that's forward thinking and it's commendable. better, more efficient and more accurate control of capital flows should be our priority. we need to know where we are, who is responsible for the control of the finances, how they are being used and how they are being spent.
mr. chairman, please! congratulations to the rapporteur, to the shadow rapporteurs. i would like to make a few comments which were also influenced by this debate. this may seem trivial to some of you, but i want to remind you that the stock market crashes during the crisis were the result, not the cause of the problems. the reason for these sharp decreases was the excessive risk taken by the market participants and the decreases were a reaction to the losses they had incurred. sometimes prices have to fall to reflect the true value of a stock or a bond or any other instrument. however, it is important that these falls do not lead to panic or excessive hesitation. that's why this regulation is so important. i am therefore pleased that it in my view responds to the challenge, as a situation in which supervisors have full information on short positions is the most appropriate situation. this will enhance the quality of supervision and the trust in this type of institution. but i'm not sure that the same thing will happen if we make this information public. i hope that this will not have the opposite effect to what is expected, for example that the knowledge of the number of open short positions will increase the willingness of investors to follow this trend more strongly. as far as cdss are concerned, i'm not sure that banning uncovered cds transactions is the right response to what's been happening with greek bonds. there is no - i don't know of any - convincing evidence that cdss have caused greater volatility or increased the interest rates on distressed countries' bonds. the markets for cds contracts are, please remember, many times smaller than the markets for the bonds of the countries they target. so it's hard to believe that this fact affects you in this way. even so, i could agree that the ban is justified if it were not for the fact - as mr kamall has mentioned, among others - that empty cdss actually cover other transactions that are not taken into account.
on behalf of the ecr group. in today's increasingly mobile world, the protection of personal data is an essential tool to ensure citizens' security and freedom to move freely within the european union. a well-organised and trust-building protection system promotes increased activity and contributes to economic and social development. the proposal to set up an agency to oversee all three existing information systems seems interesting, since the management of large-scale information systems requires the responsibility of a specialised institution. however, it is important to ensure that all member states are represented on the management board. for the data protection system to be effective, the individual solutions must be applicable to all countries. the agency should have an important role in ensuring the security of networks and data transmission by tackling increasingly common threats. the european data protection supervisor should be able to exercise his or her functions in accordance with the rules and procedures laid down in this regulation. i hope that this system will allow for more efficient data exchange and more secure data processing and sharing.
the union's budget support to developing countries is of particular importance. not only the positive effects but also the negative effects must be considered. this support has undoubtedly a direct impact on the development of economic potential. however, we must not forget the potential risks associated with budget support. these include difficulties in carrying out monitoring in countries outside the european union and possible irregularities in the allocation and use of funds. but i think that support is very important and should be continued. it is also indirectly in the interest of the european union. it results in much faster economic growth in the assisted countries and thus contributes to the improvement of their economic situation, which, through trade, will also have a positive impact on the member states and their markets. the measures envisaged will allow the internal situation in the inflamed regions to stabilise and the poverty rate to be significantly reduced. this help is important. but we must try to control and monitor better the funds coming out of the community so that they really support economic development and are not used for undesirable purposes.
member of the commission. − mr president, the commission very much welcomes this own-initiative report on energy infrastructure priorities for 2020 and beyond. it is a topic that is of course very high on the agenda and i would like to thank the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs for their commitment and constructive cooperation. energy networks are at the heart of our energy system. without secure intelligence and sustainable energy networks we cannot meet our climate goals and our energy targets in europe. within the next decades our energy system will therefore need to go through a deep transformation process that will bring huge challenges but also opportunities in the way we generate, transport, distribute and consume energy. in almost any possible future scenario, energy infrastructures will play the key role as a catalyst enabling us to meet our emission reduction objectives. furthermore, as the european council in february confirmed, they will also be crucial in ensuring that solidarity between member states becomes operational, that alternative supply routes materialise and that renewables will develop. the new eu energy infrastructure policy is needed to change the way in which networks are planned and developed in the european union. this is why the european parliament’s own-initiative report on energy infrastructure is so timely and important. in november last year the commission adopted a communication outlining our vision for such a new policy, the strategies and priorities to be pursued, and i would like to recall here what is needed. we need to build grids connecting the huge offshore wind energy potential in the northern seas to consumption centres in northern and central europe. we need to diversify our gas supplies, sources, counterparts and routes with the construction of the southern corridor. we need to develop interconnections in south-western europe with a view to integrating renewable energies and increasing the flexibility of gas flows in the region. we need to fully integrate the baltic electricity and gas market into the european market, thus ending the isolation of energy islands, and we need to strengthen the regional network in central-eastern and south-eastern europe. we need now to move from priorities to concrete projects of european interest, from plans on drawing boards to consultation, permit granting, financing and construction on the ground, and that is why our forthcoming legislative proposal on energy infrastructure will be so important. an essential element when implementing infrastructure policies is ensuring financing. it is estimated that over eur 200 billion are needed in the coming years, and not all this investment will just happen by itself. last week, as you know, the commission adopted our proposal for the next multiannual framework; it provides for eur 9.1 billion to be dedicated to energy infrastructures for the period 2014-2020 as part of a common infrastructure fund. this acknowledges the need for specific eu funding for energy infrastructures in order to deliver on our common energy and climate targets but also to ensure continued and secure supply of competitive energy to all european citizens. the commission warmly welcomes the european parliament’s support for a fund such as outlined in your resolution on the mff. the commission also appreciates the recommendations, including in the report discussed today, regarding the prioritisation of energy infrastructure projects, the acceleration of permit-granting procedures and better involvement of interested stakeholders as well as the regulation of cross-border infrastructure and financing. we will take all this into due consideration in the process of developing the forthcoming legislative proposal for a regulation on energy infrastructure development, which is scheduled for the autumn of this year. we look forward to cooperating with the parliament on this new proposal and to your support in the efforts to develop the grids europe needs for 2020 and beyond.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, infrastructure priorities should be used to create optimal energy networks in the eu's single market. the report focuses on the assumptions to be maintained. these are: ecology and climate protection, transmission efficiency and savings, competition and solidarity, security of supply, financing, cooperation between agencies and a 10-year planning period. on this basis, the market forces themselves are to create a common market infrastructure agreed with the member states. i don't think it would lead to optimal solutions. a draft vision agreed with the member states is needed. i have a few comments for the report. firstly, in paragraph 5, the rapporteur warns against 'developing infrastructure between the eu and third countries' because this could encourage the risk of co2 emissions leakage. i don't agree with that. european networks must be ready to receive energy from outside or to export it. the commission's intervention in these matters is inconsistent with the wto arrangements. secondly, european infrastructure must take account of the existence of time zones as well as climate zones. thirdly, the flow of wind energy from the north to the south requires special new networks, not only over the north sea but also over the baltic. thank you, sir.
in writing. - mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the external dimension of the eu's energy policy is one of the priorities of the polish presidency. integrated and secure energy networks are a key requirement not only for the union's energy policy objectives but also for its economic strategy. the eu needs a fully functioning internal market in this area. the provisions stipulate that the internal energy market, which will ensure the free flow of gas and electricity between eu countries and the connection of energy islands to the infrastructure, should be completed by 2015. with the need for imported raw materials growing, the eu is building a common energy policy to avoid crises like last year in the future. new transmission routes and interconnectors between countries, as well as the search for alternative raw materials, sources and supply routes, are to be the basis of energy security and solidarity among its members. poland is an important part of this system, but the country's energy infrastructure is in a state of slow degradation. polish power plants, transmission and distribution networks are decapitalised by more than 70%. in poland, with its coal-based economy, it has been possible to take account of the use of indigenous fossil fuel resources, i.e. coal, as well as shale gas. in poland, more than 90% of electricity is produced from coal. mines are profitable, which is an exception in the eu.
in writing. ensuring energy security in the european union is one of the greatest challenges facing the community. we've been debating for years whether or not to do this. however, its main objective, i.e. to become independent from russian exports, has not yet been achieved. to change this, the union needs significant investment in energy infrastructure. the construction of new transmission networks is becoming necessary. our priority must be the construction of the nabucco pipeline and the north-south pipeline. the implementation of these projects will make it possible to become independent of russian blockades and energy blackmail. this will help to reduce gas prices and strengthen the competitiveness of national economies. the construction of these routes will also be an expression of the european solidarity in the field of energy, so necessary in the last difficult period for the community. another extremely important element in the construction of europe's energy independence is the creation of the so-called polish part of the odessa/brody pipeline. the project would allow the transport of caucasian oil to central and eastern europe. this would increase competitiveness and lower prices. this investment is also in line with the eastern partnership's vision of joint energy initiatives. the report also makes little mention of financial support for the construction of further hydrocarbon storage facilities. their establishment is necessary to extend the safety period to a minimum of 120 days.
in writing. energy security is a recent buzzword, and one that is being repeated across the eu institutions. it is not just about access to energy resources, but also about efficient transmission and distribution infrastructure. the lisbon treaty has recently highlighted the need to build energy solidarity in europe in this area. this should be exploited and long-term strategic infrastructure plans should be implemented. in particular, energy connections between eu member states should be increased and alternative, strategic routes built. the interconnectors are an important part of the energy puzzle. they allow the free movement of hydrocarbons between member states. they protect them against attempted energy blockades by exporting countries and enable the price of energy produced to be stabilised. it is therefore of the utmost importance that the union provides financial support for the construction of such projects. investing in energy security also means investing in the development of new technologies. they reduce environmental impact and make better use of conventional energy sources such as coal. therefore, in the face of a restrictive climate policy, the union should actively support ccs projects, especially in countries where coal is a significant contributor to energy production.
the rapporteur. - mr president! - what are you doing? the report we are voting on tomorrow is important for the future of european union development cooperation. why would you do that? in october, the european commission will present a communication on the future priorities of european development policy. the commission will also present a legislative proposal for a future development cooperation instrument at the end of the year, and a further high-level forum on aid effectiveness will be held in busan, south korea. the busan forum is one of the development priorities of the polish presidency. it is therefore a good time for parliament to set out its own expectations for the future development policy of the union. the basis for this discussion and our report is the green paper on inclusive growth and sustainable development presented by the european commission last year. we have reached a broad political consensus in the committee on development and we agree with many of the proposals put forward by commissioner piebalgs and the commission as a whole. we believe that development cooperation must be more impact-oriented and more results-oriented than it has been in the past. but that doesn't mean we want to absolutize the metrics. we must avoid focusing on countries or sectors that are easy to reach, rather than on those where the needs are greatest. we must remember to help the poorest and those who had the misfortune to be born in countries that are very badly governed. on the other hand, it is worth remembering that 72% of the world's poor live not in the poorest countries of the world, but in middle-income countries. development cooperation cannot be interrupted when a country moves from the category of the world's poorest country to the category of middle-income countries. we will also support efforts to improve coordination. we are in favour of a proper division of labour and of exploiting the strengths of each member state. we support the european union's proposal to focus more on certain areas, such as renewable energy and agriculture. these are areas where the potential of developing countries is relatively high. we would like these priorities to be targeted at the poor and their needs, and the methods used to implement them to involve small and medium-sized enterprises, to encourage action at local and regional level. two other thematic areas of particular importance are sustainable development and climate change. however, the topic that has generated the most discussion in the committee on development is the term 'inclusive growth' itself. i don't think we should be afraid of the idea. for me personally, it means growth that is on the side of the poor, in the interest of the poor, growth that has the effect of reducing social inequality. in other words, growth should be available to the poor, not just the most active. we know that this is not an easy task, that social inclusion requires many difficult tasks to be accomplished: access to the labour market, raising labour market standards, building social security systems, tax systems. these are very difficult and important tasks. the committee on development has repeatedly and on various occasions expressed the view that in formulating new tasks or principles we must not forget our previous commitments. it's the same this time. if we are to meet new challenges, old promises must be fulfilled, and this is not just a matter of moral responsibility, but also of our credibility with external partners. the increase in the effectiveness of development aid cannot therefore be used as a pretext for reducing or freezing aid to developing countries. it's very important that we be consistent in our previous promises. i thank all the members, experts, advisers and the secretariat of the committee on development for their help in preparing this report.

the introduction of a new constitution by hungary has become a pretext for left-wing and liberal circles in the european parliament to launch an extremely emotional, often unfounded and aggressive attack on hungary, ruled by the right-wing government of prime minister viktor orbán. apart from the fact that the european parliament, in discussing the constitution of a sovereign member state, exceeds its mandate and its competence, exceeds the powers deriving from the treaty of lisbon, it is striking that during this debate there was a lack of understanding of basic ideas such as sovereignty, democracy and tolerance. after all, no one can forbid a sovereign state to refer to god, christianity, or traditional values in its constitution. no one can deny that hungary has chosen this constitution by the democratic choice of the majority of the population, in free democratic elections. and finally, tolerance is respect for other views that we don't necessarily have to share. if we expect tolerance, let us be tolerant as well. i am here to address this appeal to the representatives of the left and the liberals in the european parliament.

the systematic reduction of carbon dioxide emissions is having a negative impact on the economies of countries like poland, which rely on the burning of hard coal. the ongoing decarbonisation of energy, which reflects the drive to eliminate co2 emissions altogether, could cause a significant economic recession in both developing and developed countries. the increase in energy prices resulting from the necessary changes in energy supply and related investments can have a significant impact on the economic downturn of industrial regions. the already existing ambitious emission standards for various types of motor vehicles are increasing transport costs and requiring higher investment in innovation by manufacturers. the introduction of high greenhouse gas emission ceilings will require a significant number of companies to be co-financed by the union. i therefore remain sceptical about the possibility of increasing the 20% target for reducing emissions.
greenhouse gases know no boundaries. this seemingly obvious fact seems to be overlooked by advocates of radical reductions in co2 and other greenhouse gases. well, the european union, within its own borders, is working to radically reduce its greenhouse gas emissions, but it's turning a blind eye to the fact that other countries, like china, india, the countries of the former soviet union, are not going to do it at all. they're increasing production and increasing emissions in parallel. what are the consequences of such a policy on the part of the european union? well, it only causes production to be moved from europe to countries outside the european union, so jobs are moved, we lose taxes. but carbon-intensive production is still going on in china, in india, in south american countries. so there's still as much carbon dioxide in the atmosphere as there was, if not more. this is the road to nowhere.
mr. chairman, please! it is a good thing that today parliament rejected the demand to increase co2 emissions by 30%. the 20% discount is already a kind of madness. there is no scientific evidence that humans are the dominant cause of global warming. nature itself is regulating climate change. sometimes it's warmer, sometimes it's colder. so greenland, which is the green island by name, is now under ice. one volcanic ash plume can produce more co2 than the national economies of some european countries produce in many years. so why bleed when europe emits 15% of the world's co2 and the world doesn't want to cut it? for countries like poland, where 94% of energy production is based on coal, adopting this package would be suicide. it could mean that poland would have to contribute to the reduction of co2 emissions more than the overall net amount it would receive from the european union under the structural funds. i hope that today's decision is a step in the right direction: just as we are going to get away from 30%, we are going to get away from 20%. the polish presidency should make this issue a priority.
