acting president of the council. - mr. speaker, the house! 219 years ago in paris, on july 11, 1792, the national assembly issued an appeal, and the appeal began with the words "la patrie est en danger". i think that today we have no doubt, we can have no doubt - and i will say this in french - que l'europe est en danger. two months later, a brief skirmish took place at valmy, and the french republic was saved. it was september 1792. we are still a long way from that victory, and i would like to draw attention today to the threats facing europe, ourselves, parliament and the institutions. first of all, i think we have to say clearly, unequivocally, that if it were not for the necessary intervention of the european central bank in august of this year, an intervention that was fully justified from the technical, legal and political points of view - i will return to these three elements in a moment - we would not be looking with alarm at the coming hurricane today, we would already be in the middle of it. i have no doubt that in those hot days, the european central bank, and in particular its president, jean claude trichet, saved europe. the technical justification for the intervention, which started then and is still ongoing today, is quite clear and also constitutes a legal justification. the level of uncertainty, the level of fear that exists in the markets due to the fear of giant shocks that could naturally sink europe, prevents the normal functioning of monetary policy. how can the central bank influence and ensure price stability if the normal channel of transmission, which is the setting of interest rates, the supply of money by the central bank does not affect the actions of either european families or european entrepreneurs, or of course, most importantly, fundamentally, the behaviour of european commercial banks. all these players in european economic life are aware of the risks and therefore do not know whether to hamper money, which prevents the normal functioning of the transmission mechanisms, or to get rid of money, which could cause dangerous inflation. in this uncertain environment, the central bank's first obligation must be to safeguard transmission mechanisms and to safeguard stability. for this we must not only be grateful to the european central bank, but also stand firmly and clearly behind its decisions. (laughter) i think it's also worth thinking about what would happen if we let the eurozone gradually disintegrate, if some countries, the poorer, the weaker, were pushed out of the eurozone, or if other countries, the richer, decided to leave the eurozone on their own. members of the house of lords are probably aware of the recent analysis published by the swiss bank ubs. according to these calculations, if a poor country, a country in trouble, were to leave the eurozone, or be pushed out of the eurozone, the cost to that country could be 40 to 50 percent of gdp in the first year, and then on a scale of 10 to 20 percent of gdp per year. if a rich country were to decide to leave the euro, the cost would be 20 to 25 percent of gdp in the first year, and then gdp would be permanently 10 percent lower than it is now. these may seem like abstract numbers. let's think about what would happen to unemployment in richer countries, in a country like germany, or if a large eurozone country's budget were to become insolvent, or if that country were to leave the eurozone. of course, we don't know exactly what those effects would be, but i think the unemployment rate of well over 15% is the minimum we could fear in such a situation. moreover, it can also be considered that the very continuation of this crisis in this vague, unfinished form, will also inevitably cause, if it were to continue in this way, and of course it is doubtful whether such a state of unresolvedness of this crisis is possible, but if this situation were to continue for a year or two, then we must expect a very, very significant increase in unemployment even in the richest countries, perhaps even a doubling. poland, therefore, as a presidency and as a state, fully supports all efforts to overcome this crisis through further integration of the euro area. but we must remember that this process should not be used to create a two-speed europe. of course, we must save europe at all costs, but we should only do what is necessary within the framework of the 17 to save the euro area and therefore to save europe, because let us not be fooled, if the euro area were to collapse, europe would not survive for long after such a shock with all its dramatic political consequences. that is why i would like to end by calling for the swift adoption of the six-pack of laws. the differences between parliament and the council are now really minimal. we need to send a clear signal that we are able to work together and quickly bring the six-pack of legislation to a close. i'll end with a personal anecdote. last week at the airport, i met a colleague who worked with me in the early years of poland's transformation in the ministry of finance. today he's the president of a big polish bank. we were talking about the eurozone crisis. he said, "you know, after such economic, political upheavals, it's rare that after 10 years there's not also a war disaster. i'm seriously considering getting my kids a green card in the united states. ladies and gentlemen, the house! we can't let that happen.
member of the commission. − mr president, i welcome this opportunity to debate the measures that are urgently needed to respond to the turmoil in the euro area and on the global markets. we are confronted with the most serious challenge of a generation. this is a fight for the jobs and prosperity of families in all our member states. this is a fight for the economic and political future of europe. this is a fight for what europe represents in the world. this is a fight for european integration itself. we must acknowledge the reality. our citizens, the markets and our partners in the world have not yet been convinced that we are capable of taking on that fight and winning it decisively. in the cacophony of criticisms, counter-criticisms, magic bullets and miracle panaceas that are proposed on a daily basis the truth has been drowned out – that solid, visible, concrete proposals have been made. they have been agreed upon but they have taken too long and have not yet been fully delivered. so my first concern is implementation of what we agreed. that is why it is now imperative that we demonstrate our joint resolve to act upon our decisions without delay. now is the time to prove our full commitment to the principles of solidarity and responsibility. all euro area member states have made commitments and are making efforts to put in order their public finances and to implement economic reforms that are indeed a precondition for growth. all of these member states must now demonstrate in a convincing way that they are serious. it is not enough to make plans. it is action that counts and those euro area member states that are providing the assistance so crucial for the survival and stability of the euro must also clearly show that they are determined to deliver support to countries that implement their programmes, as they have agreed. they must acknowledge that this is also to their advantage. supporting the euro is not just an act of solidarity towards others. it is an act of self-interest. none of this is easy and we in the european institutions must recognise that. we must make the case and persuade our citizens why they should give their support. national politicians need to do much more to explain the benefits that the euro brings and we in the european institutions have a special role to play. we must do more together to make the case and i count on you to do so in your countries as well. reassurance for our citizens, for investors and for our world partners can only come from the conviction that a comprehensive approach is being delivered in the short, medium and long term. so what is needed now in the short term? first of all, the implementation of the package agreed on 21 july 2011 by all euro area heads of state and government, the president of the european commission and the president of the european central bank in the presence of the imf. it is an important package which includes measures to increase the flexibility and effectiveness of the efsf that will help to ensure financial stability. it foresees lowering lending rates, extending the maturities and allowing the facility to do more than intervene only in a precautionary way, by allowing it to intervene on the secondary markets. these decisions are important but they have not yet been implemented. the obstacles raised by some in implementing the crucial decisions already in the days and weeks following the meeting exacerbated the extraordinary developments in the sovereign bond markets during august. of course, the fact there were also difficult moments on the other side of the atlantic, creating doubts regarding the situation of the united states of america, was also a major factor aggravating the general very negative investor sentiment. this also reflected an unabated concern among investors that the euro area is incapable of responding effectively to its own crisis, because it takes too long to enact its own decisions. we have to recognise that sometimes there is a real problem between the speed of the markets and the time we take to make democratic decisions. markets are impatient and democracies are usually slower. the commission worked tirelessly through the summer to support the work necessary to implement the decisions. both commissioner rehn and i came to brussels to drive this work forward. therefore i expect all euro area member states to make good on their promises and urge them to ratify the 21 july agreement by the end of september. last weekend, the greek government took significant steps to deliver on their commitments. i urge greece to finalise these efforts together with the troika. the perspective of recovery and growth should be made a national cause. another urgent priority is the six-pack on reinforced economic governance. i talked about the delivery gap. it is now almost one year since the commission put forward ambitious proposals to strengthen governance of euro area economies. after all the talk, we are now very close to what the commission originally put on the table. the european parliament has played a decisive role in keeping the level of ambition of these proposals. i salute you for that. i would now ask the co-legislators to adopt this package as a matter of urgency. part of the leadership we must provide means being honest with our citizens that we are also addressing the structural problems europe faces. the crisis that we are facing is the result of competitiveness problems. within the european union – and also within the euro area – some member states have been lagging behind others, which has led to greater imbalances. the same types of imbalances have also built up worldwide. this has resulted in an accumulation of debts and deficits that are simply not sustainable and have been further aggravated by the financial crisis. to tackle the crisis, we must correct the excessive deficits and debts in a determined and sustainable way. this is the only way to create a union of stability and growth and it can only be done convincingly through the community method. we have a duty to learn the lessons of the crisis and to focus on the creation of growth and jobs. at the top of the agenda is the need to build a strong economy and not to use fiscal or monetary stimulus to live beyond our means. we must look at the reforms needed to correct these imbalances so as to create growth and jobs for the future. growth is key. we must use all instruments available to promote growth. in the european union we have some instruments, from the agenda 2020 to the single market act, to promote sustainable growth. europe needs to reform to deliver the good jobs, the better healthcare and the comfortable retirement that all europeans aspire to. the purpose of reform is to strengthen our social market economy; to deliver a fair society where everyone has a chance in life and nobody is left behind; and to equip all europeans with the skills, talents and opportunities to prosper in the global economy. our impulse for reform must go hand-in-hand with our sense of fairness and social equity. a sound economy also means we need sound financial markets. they have to return to their original function of a service industry for the real economy. the development of their profits must reflect the real economy. we have presented a whole series of proposals to this end, including those on short-selling and over-the-counter derivatives. in the next weeks we will go further with proposals to tackle insider trading and market manipulation, among others, as well as measures to address concerns over credit rating agencies. as i promised, the european commission will also very soon propose a financial transaction tax. when it comes to the governance of the euro area, i am convinced we need deeper and more results-driven integration, and let me be clear: this has to be within the community system. a system based purely on intergovernmental cooperation has not worked in the past and will not work in the future. (applause) after all, this is why the community method and the eu institutions were created by the member states in the first place. the economic and monetary union cannot function properly only on the basis of decisions taken by unanimity, because if a eurosceptic fringe can determine the position of one member state and if one member state can block decisions, the result is that we are not credible. this is not about institutional positioning or power. it is about efficiency and delivery. market investors will trust us only when we can show that we are able to deliver on our commitments and in a real determined way. moreover, the independent work of the european institutions further strengthens the credibility of our economic and budgetary policies. it is only through the european institutions that the european interest of all euro area member states will be counted. it is only through the european institutions that we will avoid a fragmentation of the single market and a disconnect between the 17 members of the euro area and the european project of the 27 countries that are the european union. we must keep the euro united and we must keep the euro open. if we want to ensure democratic legitimacy for decisions taken at european level, full unequivocal respect for the role of this house is crucial. if we want european citizens to take ownership of european integration, re-nationalising euro area decisions is not the way to do it. we, the european commission and the european parliament, are the community institutions par excellence. and it is our duty to defend the collective european interest jointly. we must show that the community actors are strong, united and able to deliver. delivering also means that we need a better spirit of partnership and confidence between us – the european institutions – and the member states, their governments and national parliaments. honourable members, the signal i receive time and time again from our global partners, including in the g20, is that the world expects a more integrated europe. in the age of globalisation everybody expects europe to be stronger and united. we are a valued partner in global fora and debates and we have a significant influence on global issues such as trade and climate change because in those matters we are able to act together, united. but the fact is that our way of taking and implementing decisions in the economic and monetary union is consigning us to punching below our weight. only by acting together and maximising the benefits of our interdependence will europe reach its true potential and be able to act as more than the sum of its parts. the conclusion i draw is crystal clear: the right way to stop the negative cycle and to strengthen the euro is to deepen integration, namely within the euro area, based on the community method. this is the way to go. (mixed reactions) it is also the way for the euro area to really play the role that investors and global partners expect it to play. what we need now is a new, unifying impulse: un nouveau moment fédérateur – let us not be afraid of the word – un moment fédérateur is indispensable. honourable members, the road to recovery is long and it is painful for millions of our citizens and businesses, but it will not be made less painful by continued procrastination or by presenting as quick fixes ideas that will necessarily take time. it has become clear that we need an even greater integration of our economic and budgetary policies. there has been much debate on the need for eurobonds. today i want to confirm that the commission will soon present options for the introduction of eurobonds. some of these options could be implemented within the terms of the current treaty, others would require treaty change. but we must be honest: this will not bring an immediate solution for all the problems we face, and it will be one element of a comprehensive approach to further economic and political integration. let us not confuse these projects for deeper integration with immediate necessities. ideas that would require substantial treaty change are not going to be a substitute for greece doing its homework or for euro area countries strengthening their fiscal surveillance. we must avoid compounding the dissatisfaction in public opinion by being seen as failing to deliver overnight what we already know takes time. what we need now is for greece to fully carry out its reform programme; for the six-pack to be adopted; and for member states to ratify the july 21 agreements. what would be our credibility on deeper integration if we could not deliver the six-pack or the 21 july agreement? only by proving ourselves in this way can we regain the market and public confidence necessary to even aspire to longer-term goals, to a more ambitious euro area and to a stronger europe. the commission will continue to play its role to the full, putting the key proposals on the table that shape both the immediate and the long-term response: proposals that are ambitious, that should reflect the interests of all. what both the citizens and the investors want is political determination and economic discipline. to deliver this, we need more, not less, europe. deeper integration is part of the solution. it will happen – not overnight – but in a solid, democratic process with the participation of this parliament. i believe that with courage and wisdom the european union will – as was always the case in the past – come out of the crisis stronger. it is certainly our duty to work for that purpose. (applause)

in writing. everyone in europe is aware that the eu is at a turning point in history. the debt crisis is not only a threat to national economies, but has also exposed the weakness of the eu's institutional architecture. in this context, the community must act effectively on two fronts - institutional and economic. the crisis exposed the weakness of the multi-stakeholder crisis management system. it is difficult to identify clearly who makes decisions and who is responsible for them. the result is a multitude of conflicting messages. it seems that effective governance is only possible today at community level, because only this strategy will prevent the union from fragmenting or, in the worst case, from becoming a 'two-speed europe'. institutional reform would help to rebuild the credibility of the community institutions and restore confidence in the integration process. in the context of national economies, we talk a lot in the european parliament about debt. but we must remember that debt is not only the cause of the crisis, it is also the consequence. the debt increase is not dangerous as long as it is accompanied by economic growth. if it were not for the lack of competitiveness, which is reflected in the persistently weak economic growth of some countries, no one would be talking about a crisis today. what we need are reforms that allow for debt reduction, but also reforms that provide long-term financing for growth. stability of public finances is not enough in the long term, we need sustainable economic growth.

in writing. − the main objective of this regulation is to organise the european energy market in such a way that its integrity and transparency will exclude the monopolistic or oligopolistic tendencies of large energy corporations. they lead to a disincentive to innovative energy-efficient solutions, which may have a negative impact on the situation of the final customer. this is to prevent speculative activities and to avoid, among other things, the risks that arise from abuses, especially in the derivatives market. the possibility of speculative declaration of the need to purchase energy should be limited where it cannot be immediately taken over and transferred and where there is no financial possibility to carry out this transaction. the transparency of the energy market also requires full information on actual prices, which is a sine qua non for fair play. the regulation does not include new forms of energy trading, such as capacity payment, which would prevent speculation. the costs of transporting the energy are not taken into account in the pricing of the energy (nodal pricing), which makes the total costs inappropriate. the data, even the so-called sensitive ones, should also be made available to selected scientific institutes for independent analysis. for these reasons, and considering that this regulation needs to be improved, i abstained.

in writing. − on 14 september 2011, a vote was held on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on energy market integrity and transparency, which i supported. in my view, a sectoral approach to the energy market is needed, which requires different regulatory cells, while maintaining principles consistent with financial market regulations. i believe that wholesale energy markets should be made more transparent by introducing a register of market participants. unfair practices affect the level of energy prices. market participants should report data on their (wholesale) transactions to the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators. in addition, the national control authorities should cooperate with the agency.

in writing. - homelessness affects people in all eu member states. but it turns out that we're still not doing enough to prevent it. i fully support the design of this strategy. i just hope that it will not be another one of the many documents we have adopted and that, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, we will be able to lift at least 20 million people out of poverty by 2020.
in writing. − on 14 september 2011, a vote was held in strasbourg to adopt a resolution on a european union strategy to tackle homelessness. i believe that homelessness and the social problems of the poor are important issues to which the union should devote more attention. the right to decent living conditions is a right guaranteed by, among others, the charter of fundamental rights, and therefore appropriate measures should be taken to prevent homelessness in the countries of the european union. homelessness is one of the most serious forms of poverty and deprivation and has increased in recent years in many member states. the resolution calls on member states to achieve the goal of ending street homelessness by 2015. an ambitious, integrated eu strategy to tackle homelessness, based on national and regional strategies, should also be developed, with the long-term objective of ending homelessness as part of a broader strategy for social inclusion. i think that there should be a way to monitor the progress of the fight against homelessness, which would certainly help to fight it. these arguments led me to vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! homelessness is a widespread problem, not only in europe but also worldwide. last december, the european parliament adopted a written declaration on an eu strategy to tackle homelessness to support member states in developing effective national strategies in line with, inter alia, the europe 2020 strategy. i believe that we should have an active programme to combat poverty and social exclusion and, above all, to support actions to identify effective solutions to the problem of homelessness. the eu's strategy to tackle homelessness supports these actions, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the call for an eu strategy to tackle homelessness. homelessness is a problem today that affects all countries of the union and therefore needs to be addressed internationally. only coordinated action at all levels - local, regional, national and international - can make progress in tackling homelessness. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and the binding character of the charter of fundamental rights, the union and the member states are to respect 'the right to social and housing assistance to ensure, in accordance with the principles laid down by union law and national laws and practices, a decent existence for all those who lack sufficient resources' (article 34 (3)). the european year against poverty and social exclusion is therefore a time for concrete action. we need both local and regional strategies to combat poverty and a common 'catalogue' for the exchange of best practice at international level. the eu's strategy to tackle homelessness should focus on promoting high quality services for homeless people. it should cover urban planning, housing and social policy.

in writing. africa needs more eu aid. a severe drought has affected nearly 11 million people in kenya, ethiopia, somalia and djibouti. in these countries, more than three quarters of the population are employed in the agricultural sector, which accounts for only one third of sub-saharan africa's gdp. that's why every crisis on this scale involves the tragedy of millions of people. the last two years have been the driest since the 1950s. food prices, especially grain, have risen by over 240%. this increase, which has been ongoing since june 2010, has already pushed 44 million people below the poverty line. the basic needs of millions of people in this region cannot be met. lack of access to clean water, nutritious food, and health care is a daily reality for more than half of sub-saharan africans. the situation is expected to worsen further in the next three to four months. due to the very weak and late harvest, we can expect a possible improvement as early as next year. it is therefore urgent to increase both the emergency humanitarian aid to the regions in need and the long-term investments to combat the effects of drought. better use of resources and investment in infrastructure and local coordination, as well as contingency planning, including increasing grain and seed stocks and repairing water reservoirs, are important.

draftsman of the opinion of the committee on industry, research and energy. - madam president! - what are you doing? i am speaking today on behalf of mr andrzej grzyb, rapporteur for the itre opinion committee on the future of the european union's trade policy. the rapporteur drew particular attention to the need to maintain equal access for companies in the european union and beyond when markets are opened and to place particular emphasis on access by eu companies to public procurement markets in third countries. the opinion also stresses the strategic importance of access to the world's natural and energy resources for europe's security. this accessibility should be guaranteed by the relevant provisions of the international agreements of the european union. markets should be opened in such a way as not to undermine the competitiveness of union undertakings and to protect them against unfair competition. the measures adopted should also prevent pressure to move the activities of these operators outside the common market area. these issues are of particular importance for small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the most vulnerable to unfair practices and which need to be guaranteed the opportunity to grow and compete in the global market. i am glad that most of these demands have been incorporated into daniel caspary's report.
in writing. world trade benefits all its participants. i therefore believe that we must continue to work towards the removal of barriers and restrictions. however, liberalisation also has its limits, which arise from the need to maintain a balance of benefits between the parties to the exchange. trade policy must meet certain criteria - in particular, that imported goods comply with european requirements in terms of safety standards, social issues, but also production conditions and environmental impact, as this is the basis for maintaining competitiveness. this is particularly important given the fact that the european producer is facing huge costs related to environmental compliance, working conditions and wage levels. the trade strategy is an important element of the broader development strategy. it is of additional importance in the face of the economic crisis, and trade conditions established at wto level must therefore assume equality in the level and scope of trade. i would also like to draw attention to the extremely important problem of unity and solidarity in the eu in trade with third countries. we have too many examples of our partners dividing the union by offering preferential conditions to only selected member states. the common market requires us to be uniform in our external trade.

in writing. − in building europe's future, we must pay attention to the development of scientific research and invest in innovation, because these fields contribute to job creation and to the improvement of the quality of life of citizens. high technologies and innovative solutions available to smes will make them more competitive on the world market and thus create additional jobs. that is why i voted in favour of the marisa matias report on eu funding for research and innovation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on eu funding for research and innovation. as a member of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, i wanted to draw attention to two things in particular: firstly, the need to increase the number of women in senior positions in research institutes and research projects. here, the pattern is always the same: the higher the rank in the scientific hierarchy, the fewer women. i therefore support the initiative to appoint at least one female professor to university decision-making bodies, especially to staff recruitment committees. i also support greater support for women who return to scientific work after giving birth, and for those who combine their working life with child-rearing. i'm proposing a pool of grants, scholarships, research programs geared exclusively to women. i also call on the commission to increase the number of women entrepreneurs in the competitiveness and innovation framework programme. i also support the commission's initiative to promote women's entrepreneurship and create an environment conducive to the development of women-led businesses, the so-called european network of women's entrepreneurship ambassadors.
in writing. - i believe it is very important to combine multidimensional activities for industrial development and research. in the face of increasing globalisation and the crisis that accompanies it, maintaining competitiveness is a major challenge, and research and innovation are the most important elements of this process. at the same time, the financing of these programmes at national level leads to duplication of procedures. more efficiency could be achieved by acting at a higher level at union level. integration and the proposal of a common financial framework are needed to make effective decisions to secure the common future in the most effective way. equal opportunities are also an important factor in consolidating europe, but not the only one. one of the key objectives would be to increase investment, especially for new countries which, as mentioned in the report, require significant assistance to increase investment to the required 3% of gdp, including not only short-term but also long-term objectives. the involvement of those regions and countries which are not beneficiaries of european programmes in this field should be encouraged and small and medium-sized enterprises should be supported. the social dimension of research and innovation is also worth noting. there is a need for direct communication with society, for example through education or the promotion of science, to encourage and, in a way, awaken europe's potential. in addition, procedures should be simplified, not only to facilitate the use of the programmes, but also to provide additional financial opportunities.
in writing. − the european schools are primarily a project to provide education in the mother tongue for children whose parents have left their own country. they also promote multiculturalism, learning in several languages at the same time, and a mobile, dynamic education system that makes it easy to adapt to the education model in the home country when the family decides to return from emigration. these establishments should be equitably co-financed by the member states, which also delegate teachers from their language sections. financing systems should be flexible enough to take account of emerging economic disruptions, but cuts caused by the financial crisis cannot be allowed to disrupt the development of young europeans.
in writing. the european union, as such, must contribute to the development of quality education and, above all, to cooperation between member states. i believe it is important to encourage member states and regional authorities with legislative powers in the field of education to promote the concept of a european school in their territories by organising awareness campaigns on european education. in addition, investing in young people should be our priority, which is why i voted in favour of the jean-marie cavady report on the european school system.
in writing. - i voted with satisfaction to accept the document. the european schools system has been in existence in europe for over 50 years and its model is very inspiring. more and more educational establishments are trying to meet the demands of the present and to educate children and young people in a comprehensive way, oriented towards the development of talents and skills. this should be the primary objective of modern education, and its achievement requires specific legal solutions and a clear system of funding. in poland, european-style classes are becoming increasingly popular, where students are educated in the para-university system. many universities already have courses taught in a foreign language, and at a few universities, studying (non-philological courses) is possible only through the knowledge of a foreign language. we are therefore at the beginning of a journey which will mean major changes in the european education system for the benefit of future pupils and students.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the future of eu cohesion policy. i stress the need to simplify and make more flexible eu and national rules and procedures for raising funds. the current level of complexity of the programmes does not allow for effective control of how the money is spent. i pay particular attention to ensuring that beneficiaries of eu funds have constant, free and easy access to information, advice and training. i support the proposal to set up an eu-wide cooperation programme for the exchange of information between high- and low-use regions to facilitate the dissemination of good practice. i also support the idea of creating an online platform for the exchange of good practice for beneficiaries, local and regional actors and government institutions. it is also important that future funds, in particular the globalisation fund and the european social fund, take into account the current socio-economic challenges, in particular the economic crisis. member states should better inform about the resources of the funds and simplify national procedures for their mobilisation. to this end, i am in favour of the creation of so-called 'european single contact points' to help both local authorities and eu citizens prepare their applications for funding from the funds.
in writing. − in the face of the natural and man-made disasters that are affecting europe and the world, the european union should coordinate the actions of its various institutions to be able to help victims as effectively as possible. the creation of a crisis response centre is a good move, which i hope will improve and accelerate the response of the emergency services. solidarity is the value on which the community was built, and with this in mind, we should help those in need. the cooperation of all the institutions and all the member states is essential for our actions to be effective. as one of the richest organisations in the world, we must remember the most neglected and poorest regions, which cannot cope with the disasters that beset them.
in writing. - today we voted on a very important and very good report by mrs elisabetta gardini on strengthening europe's response capacity to disasters and emergencies the role of civil protection and humanitarian aid. working in the committee on regional development, i believe that by implementing all the recommendations in the report, we will be able to improve coordination, respond at regional and national level and make the most of our strengths and resources. only such actions will reduce the impact of disasters and natural disasters. in addition, it is a good idea to merge the monitoring and information centre with echo's humanitarian crisis centre into a single entity crisis response centre, which will allow for faster information flow and better cooperation, which is why i voted in favour of the whole report.
in writing. - i supported the report on 'european disaster response capacity: the role of civil protection and humanitarian aid'. in the event of a disaster, the current union procedure is not able to provide adequate and sufficient assistance to member states. improvements in its efficiency, effectiveness, coherence and visibility are urgently needed. more efficient use of available resources will avoid additional financial and administrative procedures, especially for regional and local administrations. a more effective and early response is a much more cost-effective solution than simply repairing the damage. the consistent use of available funds for this purpose ensures effective assistance at all levels (human resources, infrastructure). sufficient aid means better identifying shortcomings and defining the eu's specific role in providing assistance to member states. i also point out the need to amend the regulation on the solidarity fund. the criteria for receiving assistance from this fund should be adapted to the specificities of the regions and the disasters. moreover, as with other funds, it is also important that they can be mobilised flexibly according to needs.
in writing. - the problem of the lack of good and efficient response systems for disasters of all kinds is unfortunately often remembered only after the fact. in recent times, we have seen many tragic natural disasters in europe and around the world. the regular torrential rains that cause floods, storms, forest fires, the icelandic volcano eruption - all these events cause huge financial losses and cause traffic paralysis. events outside europe - haiti, pakistan, japan, the explosion of a drilling rig in the gulf of mexico - have also led to thousands of deaths and negative changes in the european economy. in times of crisis, we cannot afford to duplicate the work of several member states, which means duplicating the costs and efforts of the responders in each of the community countries. we therefore need to develop a coherent, comprehensive and coordinated system for the whole of the union that is not only effective but also rational. i also call for attention to be paid to cooperation with third countries and neighbouring countries of the union. these countries should be the ones to be involved in the cooperation and coordination of actions and measures in order to exploit their potential in the most effective way, bearing in mind that disasters of all kinds have no territorial boundaries.
in writing. − the many disasters that have recently hit the community and other parts of the world require all possible action to strengthen europe's capacity to respond to disasters and emergencies. as vice-president of the delegation for relations with japan, i have been following the developments in that country with particular attention, which was hit by a major cataclysm in march this year, which was compounded by an earthquake, a tsunami and a serious nuclear power plant failure. recognising that we cannot exclude the occurrence of natural or man-made disasters, it is necessary to develop scenarios of action based on existing mechanisms and taking into account the pool of pre-determined resources. a coherent strategy, including action plans, an integrated monitoring system using satellite information, improved information flows and coordinated cooperation between member states, will certainly help to reduce environmental, social and economic damage in the event of disasters.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. it is good that the european parliament is paying more attention to the union's ability to help in the event of disasters. it is worth noting that the number of disasters reported worldwide, including in europe, has increased fivefold in the last 30 years. we must therefore do much more to help overcome the effects of increasing disasters. i believe that the european union is increasing its resources for this purpose, but the union's actual capacity is still far from sufficient. they cannot rely on resources declared on a voluntary basis by individual eu countries. the union should establish its own capabilities, at union level, which would require, for example, the provision of a fleet of transport aircraft to be used immediately when humanitarian aid is needed in the event of a disaster.
in writing. - mr. chairman, i voted to reject the report. tourism is a powerful sector, accounting for 10% of the eu's gdp, a sector of the economy and a major job creator. it is also a sector of key importance for the integration and sustainable development of the regions concerned. the need for continuous innovation in this economic sector, in particular in ensuring full access to the internet throughout the union, is also unquestionable. unfortunately, many of the provisions of the report refer to areas reserved for member states, which in my view violates the principle of subsidiarity. among other things, suggestions to simplify visa procedures for tourists, given the increasing problem of illegal immigration, could contribute to the economic crisis in some countries. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the introduction of a european tourism area is based on the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. − tourism is one of the largest economic sectors in the modern market, providing many jobs and at the same time offering broad prospects for development. promoting europe's diversity, ethnicity and the attractiveness of its regions is a tremendous asset. many of the tourist attractions of individual countries, despite their extraordinary charm, are still not promoted among the european population, which is why it is so important to support the promotion of the regions. comprehensive information makes such areas more attractive not only to tourists but also to potential investors. that is why i voted in favour of the report, which addresses these important aspects.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe there is a strong need to create a common programme to promote europe as a valuable tourist destination in the world. it is therefore essential to create a joint action to promote a common brand 'europe' that could showcase the unique values of the member states in the world, particularly in the field of tourism.
in writing. - i voted for this report because it is the first time that the european parliament has dealt comprehensively with the development of european tourism. it is an increasingly important sector in europe, but also in my country, poland, including the kujawsko-pomorskie region, where tourism is increasing its social and economic importance. the main cities are toruń, bydgoszcz, grudziądz, inowrocław, włocławek, chełmno, tuchola, brodnica, żnin and golub dobrzyń, which are also the main cities of the region. i would like to point out, however, that we should also be more effective in attracting tourists from outside the european union, including our neighbours in the so-called eastern countries. this requires significant changes to the union's visa policy. preferences should be given to tourist groups and to individual tourists, so that they can obtain visas much more easily.
in writing. - the statistics on road safety in europe are alarming. thousands of people are killed or maimed for life because of the stupidity of irresponsible drivers. the european union is therefore making it a priority to harmonise its legislation and adapt it to new technologies. the next step is to improve the infrastructure. especially in central and eastern european countries, the quality of roads is poor and often causes accidents. it is therefore necessary to check that these countries make good use of the funds available for the construction of new roads and motorways as well as railways. modern rail transport would help to relieve the road and replace the dangerous trucks, especially for other road users. i would also like to stress the need for early education. future drivers should be taught the principles of cultural participation in road traffic as early as possible and given good role models to follow.
in writing. - on 27 september 2011, a vote was held on the report on road safety in europe 2011-2020 (a7-0264/2011), which i supported. with the implementation of the third european road safety action programme, road fatalities have been reduced by 36%. despite improvements in the road situation, 35,000 people were killed and over 1.5 million injured in 2009. we must contribute to improving road safety for the benefit of the public. the actions of traffic participants and all stakeholders should be coordinated. to this end, a european coordinator office is needed to act as a liaison for the implementation of new strategies at different levels with the support of the european commission. more concrete steps should be taken to reduce the number of casualties. reliable statistics and accidents data are key to solving the road safety problem. since citizens are largely responsible for road safety, the best possible training for future drivers must be provided and those who break the rules of the road must be severely punished. the system of penalty points should be harmonised. continuous driver education and vehicle inspections are also important.
in writing. − i am a strong advocate of improving road safety through the coordination and harmonisation of road rules and signs and the implementation of a common road safety strategy. however, i believe that the negative effects of certain proposals in this legislation would outweigh the benefits. this was the case with the idea of introducing a speed limit of 30 km/h in built-up areas, which would not only have a negative impact on the transport sector, would be incomprehensible to a large part of the public, but would also not improve safety, since such a law could simply be ignored. another proposal i could not agree with was a ban on the production of road-traffic radar detectors. consequently, i voted against the regulations.
in writing. − accident statistics on european roads have improved in recent years, but still about 35 000 people are killed and 1.5 million injured in road accidents every year. the commission estimates that only 27.5% of the objectives of the third rtd programme have been achieved. i am convinced that the legislative framework on this issue is not yet fully exhausted and that further regulation at european level is possible. the koch document contains many interesting ideas, but it is not without flaws. i find interesting, among other things, the initiatives to improve the quality of training for young drivers, to make vision tests compulsory for vehicle users, and to improve safety at railway crossings. unfortunately, i am not entirely convinced of some of the rapporteur's ideas, such as the speed limit of 30 km/h in built-up areas and on all single-lane roads in urban areas that do not have a dedicated bicycle lane (i voted against this provision). for some initiatives, neither a timetable nor a way of implementing them has been defined and, given the complexity of the problem, it is not possible to implement them at the moment. however, i have endorsed the document and i trust that the european commission will take the ideas in mr koch's report seriously and present a sound analysis of the impact of the proposals as soon as possible.
in writing. − the nirja devy report on infrastructure in developing countries highlighted, among other things, the adoption of a multilateral strategy to prevent floods in regions where there is a serious risk of flooding. this is a very important problem, considering that no other natural disaster in the world has been more destructive to property or more costly to life than floods in the last century. the flooding tragedy and its consequences affect many countries in europe and the world, which is why it is so important to have a comprehensive solution to this problem. that is why i supported the report and voted in favour of it.
in writing. − there are still around 1 billion undernourished people in the world, and rising food prices are not improving the situation. the rapporteur stresses that eu member states are still not making food security and the fight against poverty - the millennium development goals adopted at the un millennium summit in september 2000 - a priority in their policies. we need to look at food security in a broader, global context. developing countries must achieve independence and stability in the access to food for their people, and our actions should be directed towards that end. let us work to ensure a level playing field on the world market and support farmers so that they can guarantee consumers healthy, easily accessible products.
in writing. − this report originates in a request by the conference of committee chairs addressed to the constitutional affairs committee in order to clarify the position of parliament as regards the meaning and legal status of unilateral statements entered in the minutes of council meetings. several committee chairs expressed their concerns about the proliferation of such statements, in particular in the framework of the codecision procedure where they could weaken the legal force and scope of the adopted acts, and so possibly affect parliament’s will as a co-legislator.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on a new trade policy for europe in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. i believe that the forecast of weaker than planned gdp performance and the relative decline in export and import performance make a change in trade policy necessary in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. i agree with the main assumptions of the report by mr daniel caspary, member of the european parliament, that the future european strategy in the field of trade policy should take into account the specificities of the individual industrial sectors and territories of the eu and the dependence on external growth. like many other members, i expected the commission to have a forward-looking trade strategy, taking account of developments in the medium and long term. we should not rely on the mistaken assumption of maintaining the status quo in world trade. i believe that it is necessary to raise awareness among citizens of the benefits of international trade and globalisation, which is often mistakenly associated with a decline in european production and the loss of jobs. i would expect the commission to pursue the objectives of the strategy for a global europe. i also believe that a more critical analysis of the strategy in the light of current trends in world trade is needed to better understand some of the failures to achieve the objectives.
in writing. − the report addresses an important trade policy issue in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. we must conduct european trade policy in a way that encourages job creation. the right policy can be a driver of growth in europe. agricultural, environmental, poverty reduction in the european union and beyond, energy and raw material security are some of the areas that should be taken into account in the conduct of trade policy. at the same time, it should not be forgotten that this topic is one of the most important elements of the union's industrial policy. a stable european manufacturing sector must be based on fair competition. the above actions would contribute significantly to the achievement of the union's agenda for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. in conclusion, i agree with the rapporteur that the commission document shows the right direction for the community, but it lacks a real strategy for the future, which europe is particularly lacking today, in order to be able to escape from the crisis, even to a small extent.

in writing. ladies and gentlemen! there is no doubt that the european union is in a deep crisis. moreover, the crisis has not only an economic dimension, which is the most visible, but also a political, social and identity dimension. we're focused on rescuing the single currency, trying to develop a rescue plan for greece and other countries threatened with bankruptcy. but above all, we should ask ourselves: what should the union be like, soon to be 28? in focusing on economic reforms, we must not forget that our community is much broader, that we are not just an economic and monetary union. the budget crisis in some eurozone countries seems to have obscured other threats. do we see a rising tide of xenophobia in our societies? do we see our economy becoming more and more penetrated by china, and beijing playing individual member states against each other? do we have a strategy for what's happening in north africa? do we see the united states no longer a reliable and stable ally? do we have the answers to the questions that we have today, or do we have a strategy that we can implement?
in writing. today is a big day. a day when, by voting on the six-pack, the ep will speak more strongly about the crisis than ever before. the outcome of today's vote will show what our vision is for the eu and the euro area and where we are going. i believe deeply that the path we choose will be a path of stable finances, low deficits and declining debt. but we must remember that simply tightening our belt is not enough. the next decisions we will have to make will be decisions about how to increase the competitiveness of our european economy. in my view, the solutions contained in the euro plus package should be implemented as soon as possible, i.e. responsible pension reforms, wage indexation reforms, reduction of vat labour costs and the creation of a genuine common market. the next issues to be addressed are the methods of financing research, education, innovation and infrastructure.
in writing. three issues are most important in the debate on the state of the eu: 1.fundamental rights in the annual report on the application of the charter of fundamental rights the european agency for fundamental rights called for special attention to be paid to the treatment of asylum seekers, the social exclusion of roma and the protection of personal data. if the union is to continue to be proud of its role as guardian of fundamental rights, it must urgently address these problems. in addition, two eu countries, namely the current polish presidency and the united kingdom, have not fully adopted the charter of fundamental rights. 2. women equality between women and men is only a formality. in fact, women are discriminated against politically, economically, socially. they earn on average 17% less than men, occupy lower positions, have a harder time getting promoted and combining their careers with child rearing. half of european women have experienced violence, 1 to 2 million women every day. women are underrepresented in legislative and executive bodies at all levels, in the boards of banks, business organisations and large companies, and in science and research. poverty almost 84 million europeans are at risk of poverty. the fight against poverty and social exclusion must be a priority. child poverty has increased dramatically during the economic crisis. in this context, i call on the council and the commission to develop and implement a strategy to halve child poverty by the end of 2012.

member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to make the following statement on behalf of the commission. the commission welcomes the adoption of the regulation on the prevention and correction of macro-economic imbalances. the regulation recognises that the nature, importance and urgency of the policy challenges may differ significantly depending on the member state concerned and that, given vulnerabilities and the magnitude of the assessment required, the need for policy action is particularly pressing in member states showing persistently large current account deficits and competitiveness losses. it also recognises that in member states that accumulate large current account surpluses, policies should aim to identify and implement the measures that help strengthen their domestic demand and growth potential. in implementing the regulation, the commission is fully committed to respecting this approach and will ensure that macroeconomic surveillance covers countries with current account deficits and surpluses with appropriate differentiation as regards the urgency of policy responses and the type of corrective actions required.

in writing. - i would like to express my satisfaction with the adoption today by parliament of the so-called six-pack. the economic crisis, the effects of which we are still experiencing, has shown that the current system of financial discipline in the member states has failed on all fronts. the stability and growth pact, which was supposed to guarantee that the euro area countries met the convergence criteria, turned out to be nothing more than a wish list. the european commission's turning a blind eye to the long-standing breach of the pact eventually led to the single currency's biggest crisis in its history. the package of legislative measures adopted today creates a new quality of coordination between the eu economies. in my view, the key issue is to equip the eu with an instrument to respond to the excessive indebtedness of a member state. it should be recalled that, according to the maastricht treaty, the level of public debt in a euro area country should not exceed 60% of gdp. but for example, the current rate for greece is almost 150%! the establishment of a framework for controlling expenditure in member states' budgets is also a very good solution - under the package, it will only be possible to increase expenditure in proportion to gdp growth. this should prevent "countries on credit". the only government that can cause a deficit in the six-pack we have adopted is a not very rigorous system of sanctions and controls on countries that do not comply with fiscal discipline.
in writing. − in today's vote, pis meps backed six pieces of legislation to tighten control over the budgetary and economic policies of the member states, to better protect against macroeconomic shocks and to make the excessive deficit procedure more effective. it should be noted that the new instruments are not a complete recipe for the euro area crisis. moreover, there is a risk that the new competences will be used in such a way that europe's competitiveness will be lost rather than gained. the eu's member states must first of all avoid the spread of bad labour, budgetary or fiscal policies across the eu. the coming years must be a period of careful examination by poland of whether the new mechanisms have a positive impact on the competitiveness of our economies. only the outcome of this eurozone crisis test will decide poland's path to adopting the single currency.
in writing. − for the first time since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the european parliament has used its new powers in the macroeconomic field and acted as a co-legislator on an equal footing with the council of the eu. this is a double success for the european parliament and the polish presidency.
in writing. − i would like to congratulate mr karl haglund on the successful work he has done in drafting the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on implementing measures to correct excessive macroeconomic imbalances in the euro area. the report examines the european commission's proposals for improving economic governance through the development of a system of economic governance. while the commission's initial draft is to be welcomed, it should place greater emphasis on preventing ineffective fiscal and macroeconomic policies. the european parliament has complemented its proposals to correct excessive macroeconomic imbalances by requiring all member states to incorporate the provisions of the stability and growth pact into their budgetary procedures, to give the commission a greater, more independent supervisory role, and to increase parliament's supervisory functions. in order to ensure greater transparency and accountability and to put an end to political 'bargaining' within the council or between the member states and the commission, the commission and the council should undertake to justify and make public their positions and decisions at all stages of the procedure. at the same time, the report includes specific economic management components such as a percentage saving or an annual fine of 0,1% of gdp in the previous year if a member state has not taken corrective action following its negative macroeconomic assessment.
in writing. − from the beginning, i have strongly supported the six economic governance regulations, designed to prevent future budgetary and economic crises in the member states. i welcome now adoption of the package and wish to congratulate the rapporteurs and both the hungarian and polish presidencies.
in writing. − addressing macroeconomic imbalances will certainly serve to strengthen the economic order in the european union and the euro area, which has been disrupted by the financial crisis engulfing europe. improving the supervision mechanisms and enforcement measures to correct the occurring irregularities will effectively prevent the occurrence of discrepancies between member states. early detection indicators should play a very important role in this respect, as they can provide effective warning and allow more time for the necessary response. on the other hand, however, particular attention should be paid to ensuring that the instruments used, which include, inter alia, the excessive deficit procedure and annual fines, have not adversely affected the attitude and attitudes of the societies of the member states towards closer european integration.
in writing. - smart budget planning and management is the foundation of public financial stability. the financial crisis that has hit the euro area and the rest of the member states has made us aware of the need to change both the budgetary and the supervisory framework. these changes will help restore the confidence of the markets in the member states of the european union, the confidence that we have lost through our weak control of the size of national deficits. it should be noted that this cannot be at the expense of promoting sustainable growth, which is the basis for increasing employment levels and productivity and social cohesion.
in writing. − article 1 of the un universal declaration on human rights reads ‘all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. they are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood’. on 17 june 2011 the un human rights council reaffirmed the universality of this declaration by adopting a first resolution on ‘human rights, sexual orientation and gender identity’. this resolution is a significant step for safeguarding the rights of the lgbt community, for it acknowledges human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity; it calls for better protection of the rights of this community, and it recognises the legitimacy of human rights defenders working on these issues. while i welcome this positive development in the un, i remain alert to the ongoing human rights violations, based on sexual orientation and gender identity, which still take place in many countries around the world. the fact that 21 eu members co-sponsored this resolution sends a powerful message to our citizens, our colleagues and partners overseas. it demonstrates the eu’s commitment to human rights, freedom of expression and freedom of choice. these rights, ultimately, are the core values of the eu.

people (not only the unemployed, the homeless, migrants, the elderly, the socially disadvantaged, people who have suffered in various ways, but also large families and single parents) benefit from the eu's free food aid. i would remind you that more than 80 million people are at risk of poverty in the european union, including 20 million children. i know that there are thousands of local charities involved in this program, hundreds, thousands of volunteers who are giving out food to the poor. usually it is young people who do this, and they learn to help others in this way. for over 20 years, the programme has not only contributed to the objectives of the common agricultural policy, but also to the building of civil society and social development. we can say that the programme is implementing the strategic objectives of the european union 2020. millions of citizens, charities and organisations are waiting for positive news from strasbourg and brussels. i'm sure many of you are listening to this debate today. the current scheme allows food from intervention stocks to be donated to designated organisations, which distribute it to the most deprived people in the european union. the common agricultural policy has undergone a fundamental change in recent years. intervention buying as a market-regulating tool has been completely withdrawn for certain products or significantly reduced. as a consequence, the reliance of the food aid programme on market purchases has increased significantly over the years. although the programme is still running, the resources allocated to it for the coming year have been significantly reduced. there is concern that in 2013 these resources will be further reduced or even completely depleted. i would like to emphasize that the presidency is seeking to find a compromise that will allow the programme to continue in its full extent. in the council, the majority of member states support the programme, but there is a blocking minority. the countries opposed to the programme argue their position in different ways. most say that the programme is implementing social policy objectives, which are the responsibility of the member states, and therefore they believe that the european union should not support the poor from the eu budget. i'm afraid i find that difficult to agree with. i don't want to criticize these countries because that's not the role of the presidency. the word solidarity in this case means helping those who need it most. remember, participation in the program is voluntary. as the commission has repeatedly stated, there is no budgetary or legal impediment to the continuation of the programme. in the eu budget we have a reserved amount of 500 million euros a year. the cost of implementing the programme is just eur 1 per citizen per year. commissioner cioloş has explained on several occasions that the judgment of the european court of justice of 13 april 2011 is not an obstacle to a political decision. five months later, the commission submitted an amended proposal to amend the contested provision. its adoption in its present form or in a slightly modified form will solve the problem of the legality of purchases from the market. so it is up to the council and parliament. opponents of the program have no reason to hide behind legal or technical issues. let's face it, they're the ones who are responsible for the fate of this program. they can't be like a sick person who breaks a thermometer on this one. by reducing or eliminating the program, we're not reducing poverty. it will strike our europe with doubled force. let us not be ashamed of poverty, but actively reduce it. as you know, the commission has proposed that in the new multiannual financial framework the financing of food aid should be transferred from heading ii to heading i. the commission considers that this programme is better integrated into the europe 2020 strategy because of its objectives. the commission shall present a new legislative proposal in due course for the period starting in 2014. i hope that the programme will then be supported by all the member states. of course, the program will not solve the problem of poverty, but it can help to reduce it. even in the richest countries of the european union, there are people in need who are experiencing problems. poverty affects not only those in cities but especially those in small towns or sparsely populated rural areas. the ongoing economic crisis, the rising unemployment rate, the number of people who cannot meet the basic needs of life - they need help, the european union needs to help. that is why we have put this programme on the agenda for the agriculture and fisheries council in september. the last debate in the council, at the request of the polish presidency, was a public debate. any citizen could have followed her online. unfortunately, for three years, we've been at a stalemate on the council's resolutions. it is a pity that in times of crisis, when the number of people in need of food is increasing, social sensitivity, the general european solidarity of some politicians is decreasing. the issue of the food programme for the poorest will probably be discussed at the october social policy council. i would like to assure the president and the honourable members that the presidency is doing everything in our power to find a solution in the context of the ongoing bilateral contacts with the governments of the member states opposed to the proposal, both at the level of the ministers for agriculture and the heads of government. i know that some delegations are wondering whether the european council should not decide on this matter on 17 and 18 october. i shall be sending a letter to the president, mr van rompuy, in the next few days. the presidency is fully aware that the commission's proposals enjoy the strong support of many meps. many member states have also declared their support. i can only assure the house that we will do our utmost to break the current impasse and work out an agreed position in the council as soon as possible. five previous presidencies have failed to make progress and break the blocking minority, but i still believe that they will succeed under my leadership. i would like to thank this house for supporting the programme, but i would also ask you to help convince national governments and parliaments who oppose eu food aid for the poorest people in the european union. i'm counting on your commitment. the programme is a confirmation of the european union's responsibility to help its citizens who are most in need, and it promotes the idea of solidarity. millions of eu citizens know that the eu is not forgetting them in times of crisis. they can count on the help of brussels and strasbourg. i can't imagine this program not being continued in the future. it will not only damage the image of the european union and its institutions, but it will damage all of us.

mr. chairman, please! i would like to say to mr eickhout that i invite him to poland because i have lived there for several decades and have not seen the rivers dry up, and as far as co2 emissions are concerned, poland has reduced them by about 30% in accordance with the kyoto protocol, which no other western european country has done. rio+20 is a great challenge and an opportunity to develop transnational solutions that ensure economic development while meeting the needs of society and the environment. the three rio conventions, which are well known and widely discussed in the eu, on biodiversity, climate change and desertification, are the answer to related problems. the rio+20 summit should primarily serve as a catalyst for developing a coordinated approach to these three conventions, and the union should take the lead in the discussions on a coherent strategy. the summit should result in concrete actions to boost the development of a green economy, including, for example, plans for environmental costs in economic decision-making, the creation of effective mechanisms and programmes adapted to global challenges that meet the needs of developed and developing countries alike. the rio conference should not be used to promote particular party, political or ideological interests. i am thinking here of the recent attempts to eliminate nuclear energy or shale gas, now enigmatically called unconventional fuel. the energy mix, as mrs auconie said, belongs to the member states. only consensus and a wise compromise will link the rio+20 goals with the need for sustainable access to different energy sources.
mr. chairman, please! we agree, of course, that development should be as sustainable as possible. but this resolution is about something else. under the guise of balancing global development, the authors offer solutions that are either inadequate or downright harmful. what does a financial transaction tax have to do with sustainable economic growth? i would remind you that this morning president barroso had already spent the money collected from this tax, but he spent it on measures to combat the financial crisis, so it will be very difficult to spend this money again, this time on climate policy. i would also point out that the linking of the tax to specific expenditure is incompatible with the principle of the universality of the tax. the ban on unconventional oil production, which affects a small part of canada and the united states, has nothing to do with sustainable development. similarly, the slowing down or global phase-out of nuclear power has nothing to do with sustainability. the inclusion of these issues in this extremely bloated resolution means only one thing: the absence of a common position of the european union for the rio conference. the resolution also contains prescriptions that could have disastrous consequences, particularly for the poorest parts of the world's population. i mean the global demand to phase out fossil fuels and replace them with renewables. even europe's wealthiest societies are unable to afford the cost of change, complaining about its high cost. how are these costs to be borne by societies that are living on the poverty line? who's going to pay for the new grids, the new energy-supply facilities, the new facilities themselves? the resolution in this form is not acceptable, but if it is adopted it will only play a detrimental role in the coordination of european policy before the rio global summit.

mr. chairman, please! the european globalisation adjustment fund is proving to be a useful instrument to support workers who are victims of mass redundancies and need help to re-skill and find alternative employment. this is evidenced by the increasing number of applications from persons directly benefitting from this aid and the amount of financial resources involved. the extension of the fund to include those who have lost their jobs as a result of the economic crisis has proved to be a step in the right direction. as a result, the egf has become an effective instrument to complement the efforts of member states to address the deteriorating labour market situation, alongside national crisis-management measures. these two arguments, namely the increased interest in support from the fund as evidenced by the increasing number of applications and the perception of the egf as an effective tool to combat the effects of the crisis, are the strongest arguments in favour of extending its extended scope until december 2013. however, among the complaints raised by the addressees of this fund is the excessive length of time taken by the european commission to process applications. this affects the delayed effectiveness of actions and sometimes reduces their effectiveness. therefore, amendments in this respect should be considered.
