in writing. − today we adopted an important report on the annual report on eu competition policy. this is already 40 reports, because this policy is one of the basic ones in the union and is very important for the functioning of the single european market, which, as i said during the debate, is the basis for economic success in the union. i am glad that the commission, and in particular mr barroso's commission, is very active in regulating the conditions of competition in financial markets. the activities of the newly established monitoring and supervisory agencies will probably contribute to the discipline of financial markets. the european commission's actions in the area of the telecommunications market have also produced positive results. but we must be aware of the need for new regulations in the services market, as well as in the energy and food markets.
in writing. − i support the openness of the european institutions and the widest possible access to documents for citizens. while it is an expression of the right to good administration, transparency is also an excellent tool for its control. extending the definition of a document to all electronic media can greatly facilitate access to them. the practice of broadcasting parliament's proceedings online, both at plenary level and at committee level, is a good example of openness and transparency. the commission should also give a clear signal of its willingness to ensure that the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies operate in a more transparent way. blocking of public information may be manifested by various restrictions on access to documents, including at the stage of their preparation. therefore, the decision to refuse to make a document available should be based on clear and precise rules specifying specific exceptions. the citizen should be given a comprehensive statement of the reasons for such a decision. i support the resolution.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the document on the european maritime safety agency. emsa has repeatedly proven to be an important link in the european safety system. in the context of the gulf disaster, i support the proposal to extend the competence of emsa to the supervision of oil and gas platforms. i also agree with the new priorities on which we have reached an interinstitutional compromise: the realisation of the concept of a european maritime area without barriers, the promotion of maritime professions and the improvement of the safety of maritime installations. at the same time, in the context of today's debate, i would like to remind the commission of an idea i put forward some time ago. i call for the organisation of a joint european maritime training centre. the aim of such a centre would be to coordinate the adaptation of the teaching systems of maritime higher education institutions throughout the european union to the changing needs of community maritime transport.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation extending the scope of the maritime safety agency. the agency has proved to be increasingly effective in its eight years of operation. however, i would like to draw attention to the fact that the extension of the agency's work must be linked to additional financial resources. eur 154 million was provided to the agency between 2007 and 2013. now her financial prospects are completely unclear. i am therefore afraid that the legitimate scaling up of the agency will be hampered by the lack of additional resources.
in writing. - mr president! - what are you doing? the latest un estimates put the death toll at over 4,000, mostly civilians, in president assad's endless bloody crackdown on his people. once again, in recent months, we have taken up the issue of syria in parliament, which clearly shows the need to intensify efforts to stabilise the situation in the country. in supporting the resolution, i wish to express my regret at the russian and chinese veto of a security council resolution condemning the syrian regime. at the same time, i demand an immediate end to the use of violence against syrian citizens. the arab league's stance on a peaceful solution to the conflict is encouraging. i would also like to pay special tribute to turkey, which has given refuge to a large number of refugees. at the same time, i call for diplomatic action to be taken against iran, which continues to actively support the syrian regime and its brutal repression. stopping the bloodshed must be the primary objective of our policy towards syria.
in writing. - a few days ago, the so-called six-pack regulations came into force. in order for this legislative package to work as effectively as possible, it is necessary to establish an appropriate set of macroeconomic indicators and to indicate their alert levels, which require the application of preventive and corrective mechanisms, i.e. which guarantee the possibility of early detection of imbalances in the external and internal economies of the member states and allow the european commission to respond adequately. the european parliament resolution is a response to the ec's proposals on these indicators and points out areas where the commission's proposal could be improved. in particular, attention should be drawn to the insufficient account taken of spillover effects and unemployment rate dynamics. it should also be noted that the ep has not been consulted on this matter, which makes the draft resolution prepared by the econ committee the only effective way to have parliament's voice heard on this matter. that is why i voted to adopt the motion for a resolution.
in writing. - the european parliament resolution on the single transport area is a resolution with the right direction. it reflects the thinking of the european union's most important politicians. however, i would like to point out that there are still considerable differences in transport infrastructure between the east and the west of the european union. sustainable regional development should therefore be promoted, which requires a particular increase in the resources allocated to less developed areas. this effort will lead to the creation of a unified transport area after years. the european freight transport market is expected to grow by about 40% by 2013. passenger transport by about 34%. the different modes of transport should therefore not compete with each other but complement each other effectively. this requires in particular an increase in expenditure on rail transport.
in writing. - i would like to draw attention, as does the rapporteur, to the vital point that we are forgetting by blindly following the money. although we, as the european union, declare our fight for human rights and sometimes even support the victims of the struggle by sending troops, we forget about the tools we have in our hands, which we can use without spilling blood. i therefore support the suspension of the signing of the protocol amending the partnership and cooperation agreement with uzbekistan, particularly as regards the textile sector. we cannot allow thousands of children to suffer, who are used to harvest cotton. we can't afford to have that kind of hypocrisy. at the same time, dialogue with the uzbek authorities should be pursued to change the situation so that a trade agreement is also possible.
in writing. − the development of relations with the countries of central asia is of strategic importance for europe. these are dynamic developing countries, and they are very important to the world economy. four years is a good time to sum up the results of the eu strategy for the region. the regularity of meetings and the strengthening of relations between high-level representatives is particularly encouraging, especially in the face of events as important as the global crisis. the number of eu missions in these countries is also very small, with only three, so i have high hopes for the proposal to set up a regional interparliamentary forum. another important requirement is the need to increase eu funding for programmes in the region. this also involves developing a strategy for their proper absorption. i agree with the assumption that the pillars of policy towards these countries must be security, the rule of law and respect for human rights and genuine regional cooperation. i support the resolution.
in writing. − central asia is a significant regional player for many economic, political and strategic reasons. thus in 2007 the eu introduced a strategy towards the five central asian countries, aiming to strengthen and improve the structure and relations between the two regions. this strategy included high-level periodic meetings, cooperation with civil society, resources management and more. due to changing regional dynamics in central asia, caused by inter-ethnic riots, new geostrategic configurations as well as the nato operation in afghanistan, the eu has asked to review its 2007 strategy and evaluate its success. the results of this review indicated shortcomings in the 2007 strategy, as standards of good governance and respect to human rights have only slightly improved. in the current state of affairs i welcome the eu’s review and desire to reshape its approach towards central asia. yet i remain hopeful the new strategy will prioritise democracy, respect for human rights and the rule of law above any economic, energy or security interests. this is vital for yielding positive results and for maintaining the eu’s credibility. the new strategy for central asia genuinely demonstrates eu’s dedication to the region, for enforced and better cooperation can lead to significant social, economic and political achievements.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. rafiq tagi was indeed a symbol of a free media. his family, azerbaijani citizens and ngos are all calling for a real, honest investigation. remember that azerbaijan is a member of the eastern partnership, so i call on all countries and governments involved in this program to put pressure on the azerbaijani authorities. after all, it is unacceptable that citizens - i am thinking here of mr. bahtiyar hajiyev, for example - go to jail for organizing events on facebook. i myself organized a facebook event "freedom lamps" on december 10th, international human rights day, and thousands of people in krakow were able to remember this important day and the people whose freedom is being violated. we cannot allow people to go to prison for similar actions in other countries, and in the eastern partnership countries. i would like to ask that mr tagi be awarded the eastern partnership journalism prize at the eastern partnership civil society forum next year.
in writing. despite 20 years of independence and the fact that it is one of the fastest growing economies in the world, authoritarian governments and control over the social life of citizens are still being strengthened in azerbaijan. the restrictions and violations of basic human rights by intimidating and suppressing the speech of those who dare to criticize the authorities are common. independent media and opposition journalists are particularly vulnerable, often facing prison sentences for their content. the government is indifferent to their fate, as exemplified by the character of rafiq taghi. as a result of his journalistic activities, tagi was imprisoned for inciting religious hatred. his articles aroused the displeasure of muslims, who issued a fatwa condemning him to death, and the authorities did not protect him from the possibility of fulfilling these threats. a few weeks ago, rafig tagi died from injuries sustained by unknown assailants. the incident coincided with the international day of impunity and sparked protests by journalists around the world, who called for an end to the killings of their colleagues and demanded punishment for those responsible. we should show solidarity with the azerbaijani media and strive to maintain freedom of speech in azerbaijan and call on the international community to end impunity for attacks on journalists not only in this country but also around the world.
the author. - mr president! - what are you doing? it seems incredible that in the 21st century, there are still countries that exclude women from active public and economic life. in afghanistan and pakistan, women are marginalized, denied the opportunity to develop and reach their full potential. many bans, punishments, physical or psychological discrimination restricting women's areas of activity are commonplace in these countries. the situation of afghan women has improved somewhat in recent years following the fall of the taliban regime. however, the conditions of women in pakistan have deteriorated significantly due to the introduction of discriminatory regulations such as the religious sentiments protection act, which allows the persecution of women and minority groups. therefore, a review of women's rights in the domestic law of both countries should be a first step towards ensuring women's decent living conditions, including the right to professional and personal development, including the protection of women's safety in schools and at work. given the long-standing and long-standing assistance offered by the union to both countries, it is our duty not only to express concern about discrimination against women but also to call for equal treatment between the sexes.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. according to reuters, afghanistan is the number one country in the world for women's rights violations. third on this list of shame is pakistan. there is religious and cultural sanction for acid throwing, stoning, honor killings. the reason is the lack of worldview neutrality of the states. the dominant religion, which denies women many of their human rights, has a decisive influence on the situation of women. half of the women in prison in afghanistan have been convicted of so-called moral crimes, such as adultery, leaving a husband, or running away from home. ninety percent of afghan women have been beaten, raped, psychologically harassed, forced into marriage against their will. despite the intervention of nato forces, the situation of women in afghanistan has not improved, but rather deteriorated. laws designed to protect them have caused even more aggression on the part of men. we must oppose this with all our might.
mr president, at the beginning of december the international community met with afghani authorities at the bonn ii conference. afghanistan made a commitment to include the upholding of human rights commitments in its constitution, including equality between men and women, which is to be welcomed and supported by the european union. looking ahead to 2014 when the allied forces withdraw from afghanistan and afghanistan has full independence to run its own affairs, it is imperative that progress is not undone. the peace dialogue at present underway between the government and elements of the taliban should in no way result in a deterioration of the rights acquired by women, and we as the eu should give support in this matter.
mr. chairman, please! the arrest of zakariya bouguirra on november 13th is another alarming case of human rights violations in tunisia, a country that has just emerged from ben ali's dictatorship. zakaria bouguira tried to record with his phone the moment of the violent clash between tunisian police and moroccan football fans. for this he was beaten by the police and put in jail. his case has raised international concern, as it came less than a month after the country held democratic elections. we recognise the challenges of the change and will support the country's move towards a broad-based democracy, but we must also strongly protest against the acts of violence and human rights violations that we are witnessing today. the newly elected government should implement the necessary reforms as soon as possible to make tunisia a true state of law, where the principles of democracy are respected and the rights and civil liberties that should also be enjoyed by zakariya bouguirre are respected.
mr. chairman, please! the alarming fact is that the tunisian police force is using violence and human rights violations in an uncontrolled manner. tunisia must undoubtedly reform its law enforcement and judicial sectors as soon as possible. they should be covered by regulations guaranteeing respect for human rights and imposing sanctions for their violation. i particularly support the call for the creation of a national human rights council to safeguard international human rights standards. the institution could also deal with individual complaints from citizens and investigate cases of human rights violations. the european union should make the best use of its neighbourhood policy instruments to support the process of democratic transition in tunisia.
